name: *http-post*
doc: HTTP POST seam. Rebind with `binding` in tests to inject a fake transport. Tagged `^:dynamic` so concurrent tests rebinding it stay isolated per fiber.

name: anthropic-request
doc: Builds an HTTP request for the Anthropic Messages API. Optionally includes tool definitions.

name: apply-opts
doc: Merges per-call opts into cfg. Copies over keys whose value is non-nil so numeric zero and `false` propagate (e.g. `:max-tokens 0`), while an explicit `nil` is treated as 'leave the config alone'.

name: assistant-message
doc: Builds an assistant message preserving the model's tool_use blocks so the next turn can carry the conversation forward. Anthropic-only for now.

name: backoff-sleep
doc: Sleeps using exponential backoff. attempt is 0-based.

name: build-index
doc:
Builds a searchable index from a collection of text strings.

Embeds all texts and returns a vector of {:text, :embedding} maps suitable for use with `nearest`.

Options are passed through to `embed`.

name: chat
doc:
Sends a chat completion request with a list of message maps.

  Each message is a map with :role and :content keys.
  Returns the assistant's text response as a string.

  Accepts an optional options map:
    :system     - System prompt string
    :model      - Override the configured model
    :max-tokens - Override the configured max tokens
    :provider   - Override the configured provider
    :timeout    - HTTP timeout in seconds
    :base-url   - Override the API base URL
    :api-key    - Override the configured API key

name: chat-with-history
doc:
Appends a new user message to an existing conversation history, sends it, and returns the updated history with the assistant's response.

Useful for building multi-turn conversations.

name: chat-with-tools
doc:
Sends a chat request with tool definitions.

  Returns a map:
    :text       - Assistant text content (may be nil if model only called tools)
    :tool-calls - Vector of {:name :id :input} maps for any tool calls
    :stop-reason - Provider-specific stop reason
    :raw        - The full provider response body

  Options map accepts the same keys as `chat`.

name: check-response
doc: Checks an HTTP response for errors and throws if the request failed.

name: complete
doc:
Sends a simple text completion request.

Takes a prompt string and returns the assistant's text response. This is a convenience wrapper around `chat` for single-turn interactions.

name: config
doc: Current AI configuration atom. Use `configure` to update.

name: configure
doc:
Merges the given options into the AI configuration.

  Supported keys:
    :provider    - :anthropic (default), :openai, or :voyageai
    :model       - Model name string
    :max-tokens  - Maximum tokens in response
    :api-key     - API key string (or set via env var)
    :base-url    - Override the API base URL
    :timeout     - HTTP timeout in seconds (default 120)
    :max-retries - Retry attempts on 429/5xx (default 2)

name: cosine-similarity
doc: Computes the cosine similarity between two numeric vectors. Returns a float between -1.0 and 1.0, where 1.0 means identical direction.

name: default-extract-system
doc: You are a precise data extraction assistant. Return only valid JSON.

name: dot-product
doc: Computes the dot product of two numeric vectors.

name: embed
doc:
Generates embeddings for one or more text strings.

  Returns a vector of embedding vectors (one per input text).
  Uses OpenAI's text-embedding-3-small by default.

  Options:
    :model    - Override the embedding model name
    :provider - :openai (default) or :voyageai

name: embed-one
doc: Generates an embedding for a single text string. Returns a single embedding vector.

name: embed-request
doc: Sends an embedding request to the given provider.

name: extract
doc:
Extracts structured data from text using AI.

  `schema` is a map of field names to type descriptions. Each key becomes
  a field in the output, and each value tells the AI what to extract.

  Returns a Phel map with the schema keys populated from the AI response.

  Options:
    :system     - Override the system prompt
    :model      - Override the configured model
    :max-tokens - Override the configured max tokens

name: extract-anthropic-text
doc: Extracts the text content from an Anthropic API response.

name: extract-json-array-from-response
doc: Extracts a JSON array from a model response, slicing between the first '[' and the last ']' when the array isn't already at the start.

name: extract-json-from-response
doc: Extracts JSON from an AI response, handling markdown code blocks.

name: extract-many
doc:
Extracts a list of structured items from text.

Similar to `extract`, but returns a vector of maps when the text contains multiple items matching the schema.

name: extract-openai-text
doc: Extracts the text content from an OpenAI API response.

name: extract-text
doc: Extracts text from a provider response.

name: magnitude
doc: Computes the magnitude (L2 norm) of a numeric vector.

name: nearest
doc:
Finds the k nearest items to a query embedding from an index.

  `index` is a vector of {:text "..." :embedding [...]} maps.
  Returns a vector of {:text, :embedding, :similarity} maps sorted
  by descending similarity.

name: openai-request
doc: Builds an HTTP request for the OpenAI Chat Completions API.

name: openai-tools->request
doc: Converts Anthropic-shape tool defs to OpenAI's function-calling shape.

name: post-with-retry
doc: Posts with retry on 429 / 5xx up to max-retries.

name: provider-base-url
doc: Returns the default base URL for the given provider.

name: provider-env-var
doc: Returns the canonical environment variable name for the given provider.

name: provider-error-message
doc: Extracts a human-readable error message from a decoded provider error body.

name: resolve-api-key
doc: Resolves the API key from config or environment variables. Supports :anthropic, :openai, and :voyageai providers.

name: resolve-base-url
doc: Resolves the base URL: explicit `:base-url` from config, otherwise the provider default.

name: run-extraction
doc: Drives a single-shot extraction call with the given prompt and opts.

name: run-tools
doc:
Drives a tool-calling loop: repeatedly sends `messages` with `tools`,
  resolves any tool calls via `handlers`, and feeds the results back in
  until the model returns a final text response (or `:max-turns` is hit).

  - `messages`: initial conversation (vector of role/content maps)
  - `tools`: tool definitions built with `tool`
  - `handlers`: map of tool-name (string) -> fn taking the call's :input map
                and returning a value (stringified into the tool result)
  - `opts`: same keys as `chat-with-tools`, plus `:max-turns` (default 5)

  Returns the assistant's final text. Throws if a tool name has no handler
  or if `:max-turns` is reached without a final response. Anthropic-only;
  OpenAI tool loops require a different message shape and are not handled.

name: schema->json-description
doc: Converts a field schema map to a human-readable JSON description for the AI prompt.

name: schema->json-schema
doc: Converts a field schema map to a JSON Schema object for tool use.

name: schema-prop-spec
doc: Resolves a schema field value into a JSON Schema property spec.

name: search
doc:
Semantic search: embeds a query and finds the k nearest matches in a pre-built index.

Returns a vector of {:text, :embedding, :similarity} maps.

name: send-request
doc: Sends a prepared request map with retry + timeout.

name: similarity-with-mags
doc: Cosine similarity given each vector's precomputed L2 magnitude. Returns 0.0 when either magnitude is zero (and skips the dot product in that case).

name: slice-between
doc:
Returns the substring of `trimmed` spanning the first `open` char to the
  last `close` char (inclusive). Throws `RuntimeException` prefixed with
  `error-prefix` when no balanced pair is found.

name: tool
doc:
Creates a tool definition map for use with `chat-with-tools`.

  `tool-name` is a string identifier for the tool.
  `description` describes what the tool does.
  `input-schema` is a map of parameter names to JSON Schema type maps.

  The returned map is provider-agnostic; `chat-with-tools` converts it to
  the provider's native format.

name: tool-calls
doc:
Extracts tool call requests from an AI response.

  Accepts either a raw provider response body or a map produced by
  `chat-with-tools`. Returns a vector of {:name :id :input} maps.

name: tool-result
doc:
Builds a tool-result message for the given provider.

  `call-id` is the tool call id returned by the model.
  `result` is the tool's output as a string (or value that will be stringified).

  Optional `opts` can set :provider (defaults to current config).

name: truncate-for-error
doc: Truncates a string for inclusion in an error message so we don't echo the full model response (which may contain prompt content) into logs.

name: with-config
doc: Temporarily merges `opts` into the global config for the duration of `body`, then restores the previous config. Safer than `configure` for embedded use, since it won't leave global state mutated when `body` throws.

name: delay
doc:
Suspends execution for `seconds`. Accepts any number (int, float, or
  `Ratio`); sub-second precision such as `0.05` is supported.

  At the top level this behaves like `php/sleep` / `php/usleep`: it
  blocks the script for the given duration. Inside an `async`/`future`
  body (or any AMPHP fiber context) it suspends the *fiber*, not the
  whole process, so other concurrent fibers keep running and the
  delay is cancellable via `future-cancel`.

  `phel.async/delay` is **not** the Clojure `clojure.core/delay`. The
  Clojure form returns a lazy thunk that caches the result of evaluating
  `body` on first `deref`; Phel's version is a sleep primitive. They are
  unrelated. Reach for `phel.async/delay` when you want to throttle, time
  out, or compose with `future` / `pmap`; reach for `php/sleep` when you
  just want a blocking pause and don't care about fiber semantics.
example:
(delay 0.5) ; suspends current fiber for 500ms
  (async (delay 1.0) :done) ; => future that resolves after 1s
  (delay (/ 1 1000)) ; ratio collapses to a float

name: decode
doc: Decodes a Base64 string. When `strict?` is true, validates that the input contains only characters from the Base64 alphabet and returns false on invalid input (defaults to false).

name: decode-url
doc:
Decodes a URL-safe Base64 string, adding padding automatically. When
  `strict?` is true, validates that the input contains only valid Base64
  characters (defaults to false).

name: encode
doc: Encodes a string to Base64.

name: encode-url
doc: Encodes a string to URL-safe Base64 (no padding).

name: baseline-map
doc:
Reads a stored baseline as `{"ns/name" mean-ns}`. A missing or unreadable
file is an empty baseline rather than an error: comparing against nothing is a
normal first run, not a failure.

name: comparison-cell
doc:
Delta against the baseline, or a placeholder when there is nothing to
compare against. A benchmark added since the baseline was stored is `new`
rather than an improvement of infinity.

name: defbench
doc:
Defines a benchmark function.

The body is timed, not asserted. An optional option map may follow the name:
`:revs` (calls per measured iteration), `:iterations` (measured iterations),
`:warmup` (unmeasured iterations first). Anything omitted falls back to the
default. A run-wide option of the same name, such as a `phel bench --revs`
flag, overrides what the benchmark asks for.

Metadata attached to `bench-name` is forwarded to the defined function, so
`^:slow` and `^{:tags [:io]}` work here exactly as they do on `deftest`.

name: find-benchmarks
doc: Every `defbench`-defined function in `ns`, in definition order.

name: format-duration
doc: Nanoseconds rendered in the largest unit that keeps the number readable.

name: measure
doc:
Runs one benchmark and returns its result map. The benchmark function itself
is never passed on: everything downstream works off the numbers.

name: now-ns
doc:
Monotonic nanoseconds. `hrtime` is unaffected by wall-clock adjustments,
which `microtime` is not.

name: option-for
doc:
Run-wide option, falling back to the benchmark's own and then the default.

The run-wide value wins on purpose: it is what the caller asked for *now*,
typically a `phel bench --revs` flag, and a flag that a file could silently
override would be worse than no flag at all.

name: report-regressions!
doc:
Prints the regressions and returns false, or returns true when there are
none. Returning the verdict rather than throwing keeps the decision with the
caller, which is what lets the CLI turn it into an exit code.

name: rstdev
doc:
Relative standard deviation, as a percentage. This is the number that says
whether a run is trustworthy: above a few percent, a comparison against a
baseline is noise.

name: run-benchmarks
doc:
Runs every `defbench` in the given namespaces and prints a table.

Recognized option keys: `:revs`, `:iterations`, `:warmup` (each overrides the
per-benchmark option of the same name), `:filter` (substring match against
the benchmark name), `:store` (path to write the results to as a baseline),
`:ref` (path to a stored baseline to compare against), and `:tolerance` (a
percentage; when set, a benchmark slower than its baseline by more than this
makes the run unsuccessful).

Returns true when the run is within tolerance, which is always the case when no
tolerance is set.

name: slower-than-tolerance
doc:
The results that regressed against the baseline by more than `tolerance`
percent. A benchmark with no baseline entry cannot regress, so it is never a
failure: the first run after adding one would otherwise fail.

name: time-revs
doc:
Calls `f` `revs` times and returns the nanoseconds per call.

The loop is `dofor` rather than `dotimes` over a seq so the measured region
allocates nothing per rev beyond what the body itself allocates.

name: application
doc:
Build a Symfony `Application`.

  Single-arity (preferred):
    (application {:name "mytool"
                  :version "1.0.0"
                  :commands [...]
                  :default  "greet"
                  :auto-exit? false
                  :before    on-before-fn   ; receives ConsoleCommandEvent
                  :after     on-after-fn    ; receives ConsoleTerminateEvent
                  :on-error  on-error-fn    ; receives ConsoleErrorEvent
                  :on-signal {:sigint cleanup-fn :sigterm cleanup-fn}})

  Two-arity convenience:
    (application "mytool" [command-specs...])

name: arg
doc: Read (and coerce) an argument value by name.

name: argv
doc: Build an `ArgvInput` from a vector of string tokens. Positional args and `--flag=value` are parsed just like a real shell command line.

name: argv-with-stdin
doc: Like `argv` but also wires a STDIN stream so `ask`/`confirm`/`choice` prompts can be tested with canned answers.

name: ask
doc: Free-text prompt. `default` optional.

name: ask-hidden
doc: Prompt without echoing (passwords).

name: buffered-output
doc: Build a `BufferedOutput` that captures writes into a string.

name: caution
doc: Boxed caution message.

name: choice
doc: Single-choice prompt over a vector of options.

name: command
doc:
Build a Symfony `Command` from a Phel spec map.

  Spec keys:
    :name     command name, e.g. "build" or "app:build"     (REQUIRED)
    :doc      short description (shown in `list`)
    :help     long help text (shown in `<cmd> --help`)
    :aliases  vector of alternate names
    :hidden?  true = hide from `list`
    :args     vector of arg specs `{:name :mode :doc :default :coerce :complete}`
    :opts     vector of option specs `{:name :short :mode :doc :default :coerce :complete}`
    :run      handler `(fn [ctx] ...)` — ctx = {:input :output …};
              returns nil/0 for success, int for exit code.
              Uncaught `Throwable` rendered as `<error>`, mapped to exit 1.

  Modes     :required :optional :array (:args) + :none :negatable (:opts)
  Coerce    :int :float :bool :keyword :edn
  Complete  fn `(CompletionInput -> vector<string>)` for shell completion.

name: comment-line
doc: Yellow comment line.

name: confirm
doc: Yes/no prompt. `default?` defaults to true.

name: debug
doc: Write only when -vvv (debug).

name: error
doc: Red error line.

name: info
doc: Green info line.

name: info-v
doc: Write only when -v or higher.

name: info-vv
doc: Write only when -vv or higher.

name: listing
doc: Bulleted list of items.

name: note
doc: Boxed note.

name: null-output
doc: Build a `NullOutput` that discards writes.

name: opt
doc: Read (and coerce) an option value by name.

name: output->string
doc: Drain a `BufferedOutput` into a string.

name: output-contains?
doc: Test helper. Accepts a `BufferedOutput`, a string, or a map `{:out s}`.

name: progress-advance
doc: Advance by n.

name: progress-bar
doc:
Create a `ProgressBar` bound to the context output.

  Options:
    `:max`    total steps (0 = indeterminate)
    `:format` preset (:normal :verbose :very-verbose :debug :minimal) or custom string

name: progress-finish
doc: Finish + newline.

name: progress-start
doc: Start the bar.

name: run
run-with-progress
doc: Iterate `coll` and invoke `(step-fn item bar)` for each, handling start / advance / finish automatically.

name: section
doc: Sub-heading.

name: stdin-lines
doc:
Return a vector of lines from STDIN (trailing `\r\n` stripped).
  Useful for `cat data.txt | mytool`.

name: style
doc:
Return a cached `SymfonyStyle` bound to the context so successive
  `ask`/`confirm`/progress calls share state.

name: success
doc: Boxed success message.

name: table
doc:
Render an ASCII table.

  Options:
    `:style`  one of :default :borderless :compact :symfony :box :box-double :markdown
    `:widths` vector of column widths

name: title
doc: Heavy heading.

name: warning
doc: Boxed warning message.

name: write
doc: Write text without trailing newline.

name: writeln
doc: Write a line.
Returns the difference of all elements in `xs`. If `xs` is empty, return 0. If `xs` has one element, return the negative value of that element.

Auto-promoting variant of `-`. Integer results are returned as
  `BigInt`; floats and rationals pass through unchanged.

Threads the expr through the forms. Inserts `x` as the second item in the first form, making a list of it if it is not a list already. If there are more forms, insert the first form as the second item in the second form, etc.

Threads the expr through the forms. Inserts `x` as the last item in the first form, making a list of it if it is not a list already. If there are more forms, insert the first form as the last item in the second form, etc.

name: ->closure
doc: Converts a Phel function to a PHP Closure. Many PHP libraries (AMPHP, ReactPHP) type-hint `\Closure` and reject Phel's `AbstractFn` even though it is callable. This bridges the gap.
Returns the product of all elements in `xs`. All elements in `xs` must be numbers. If `xs` is empty, return 1.

Auto-promoting variant of `*`. Integer results are returned as
  `BigInt`; floats and rationals pass through unchanged.
Return `a` to the power of `x`.

name: *argv*
doc: Vector of user arguments passed to the script (excludes program name). Use *program* to get the script path or namespace.

name: *assert*
doc: Controls whether `assert` expands to a runtime check. When logical false at macroexpansion time, `assert` expands to nil and performs no runtime check, matching Clojure's compile-time `*assert*` semantics. Defaults to `true`. To disable globally, set the core binding before compilation via PHP: `\Phel::addDefinition("phel\\core", "*assert*", false)`.

name: *file*
doc: Returns the path of the current source file.

name: *hierarchy*
doc: Global hierarchy for keyword/symbol taxonomies.

name: *ns*
doc: Returns the namespace in the current scope.

name: *program*
doc: The script path or namespace being executed.

name: *protocol-type-relations*
doc:
Maps PHP class tags to the set of protocol values they implement.

Maintained in parallel with `derive`'s class -> proto-class-string entry so hierarchy queries surface the protocol value itself (the map produced by `defprotocol`) and not just its FQN string.

name: *type-tag-registry*
doc: Maps generated struct constructor functions to their PHP class tag.

Returns the nominator divided by all the denominators. If `xs` is empty,
returns 1. If `xs` has one value, returns the reciprocal of x.

  Integer division with a non-zero remainder returns a `Ratio`
  (e.g. `(/ 1 2) => 1/2`). Use `(/ 1.0 2)` or `(double ...)` for float
  division.

Alias for `rem`. Returns the truncated remainder of `dividend` /
  `divisor`. Result has the same sign as `dividend`.
Returns the sum of all elements in `xs`. All elements `xs` must be numbers. If `xs` is empty, return 0.

Auto-promoting variant of `+`. Integer results are returned as
  `BigInt` so callers get explicit promotion semantics; floats and
  rationals pass through unchanged. Equivalent to `+` for overflow
  protection (Phel's `+` already auto-promotes on overflow), kept for
  `.cljc` interop.
Checks if each argument is strictly less than the following argument.
Checks if each argument is less than or equal to the following argument. Returns a boolean.
Alias for the spaceship PHP operator in ascending order. Returns an int. Dispatches on `Ratio` and `BigInt` so numeric ordering stays correct for those types.
Checks if all values are equal (value equality, not identity).

Numeric equality comparison. Returns true if all arguments have the same
  numeric value regardless of type (e.g. int vs float); throws on non-numeric
  arguments. Unlike `=`, which is value-and-type-strict, `==` treats `1` and
  `1.0` as equal, matching Clojure's `clojure.core/==`.
Checks if each argument is strictly greater than the following argument.
Checks if each argument is greater than or equal to the following argument. Returns a boolean.
Alias for the spaceship PHP operator in descending order. Returns an int.

name: abs
doc:
Returns the absolute value of `x`.
  Throws `InvalidArgumentException` if `x` is not a number; PHP's
  permissive `abs(null) => 0` / `abs("abc")` coercions are rejected.

name: aclone
doc: Returns a shallow copy of a PHP array. The returned array is a distinct value — mutating the copy via `aset` does not affect the original, and vice versa. Matches Clojure's `aclone` for `.cljc` interop; raises `InvalidArgumentException` on non-array inputs since Phel's persistent collections are already immutable and don't need cloning.

name: add-tap
doc: Registers `f` as a tap. Every call to `tap>` invokes each registered tap with the tapped value. Returns nil.

name: add-watch
doc: Adds a watch function to a variable. The watch fn is called when the variable changes with four arguments: key, ref, old-value, new-value.
example: (add-watch my-var :logger (fn [key ref old new] (println old "->" new)))

name: aget
doc: Returns the value at `index` in a PHP array. With multiple indices, accesses nested arrays: `(aget arr i j)` is `(aget (aget arr i) j)`. Matches Clojure's `aget` for `.cljc` interop.

name: alength
doc:
Returns the number of elements in a PHP array. Matches Clojure's
  `alength` for `.cljc` interop; raises `InvalidArgumentException` on
  non-array inputs (use `count` for collections).

name: all-int-first-elements?
doc:
True when every `[key value]` pair carries a native int key. Mirrors
  `all-native-ints?`, over the decorated pairs rather than the elements.

name: all-native-ints?
doc:
True when every element of the PHP array is a native int. Mirrors the
  namesake in `seq-fns`, which cannot be reached from here: both are private,
  and this file loads first.

name: all-native-ints?
doc:
True when every element is a PHP int. Deliberately narrow: floats bring NaN
  and mixed-type comparison, and anything else is not orderable by
  `SORT_NUMERIC` the way `compare` orders it.

name: all-native-strings?
doc:
True when every element is a PHP string. `sort` with the default
  `SORT_REGULAR` then produces exactly the order `compare` produces, because
  both settle a pair of strings with PHP's `<=>`.

  `SORT_STRING` would be the obvious choice and is wrong: it compares
  lexicographically, where `<=>` compares two numeric strings numerically.
  `["10" "9" "2"]` sorts to `["2" "9" "10"]` under `compare` and to
  `["10" "2" "9"]` under `SORT_STRING`.

name: all?
doc: Returns true if predicate is true for every element in collection, false otherwise.

name: alter-meta!
doc:
Replaces the metadata on `r` with `(apply f current-meta args)`.
  Works on `Var` handles (mutates per-var metadata, surviving subsequent
  `def` redefinitions) and on atoms (mutates the atom's own meta map).
  Returns the new metadata map.

name: alter-var-root
doc: Replaces the root binding of `v` with `(apply f current-root args)`. Returns the new root value. `v` must be a `Var`; pass an atom and you get a clear error pointing at `swap!` instead.

name: ancestors
doc: Returns the set of all transitive ancestors of tag, or nil. When a hierarchy is provided, consults it; otherwise uses the global hierarchy.

name: and
doc: Evaluates expressions left to right, returning the first falsy value or the last value.

name: any?
doc: Returns true given any argument, including `nil` and `false`. Mirrors Clojure's `clojure.core/any?` — useful as a default predicate in spec / validation contexts where every value should be accepted.

name: apply
doc: Applies function `f` to the argument list formed by prepending any intervening arguments to the final collection argument.
arities: (apply f a b c d & args)

name: arity
doc: Returns the number of required parameters of the function `f`. For a variadic function this is the number of parameters before `&`. A multi-arity function compiles to a single variadic dispatch, so it reports `0`.

name: array-map
doc: Constructs a map from the given key/value pairs. If any keys are equal, later values replace earlier ones, as if by repeated `assoc`. Phel has no distinct array-map type, so the result is the same persistent map as `hash-map` — `array-map` exists for `.cljc` interop with Clojure sources.

name: as->
doc: Binds `name` to `expr`, evaluates the first form in the lexical context of that binding, then binds name to that result, repeating for each successive form, returning the result of the last form.

name: aset
doc:
Sets the value at `index` in a PHP array to `val`. Returns `val`.
   With additional indices, navigates nested arrays before setting:
   `(aset arr i j val)` sets index `j` in `(aget arr i)`.
   Matches Clojure's `aset` for `.cljc` interop.
   This is a macro because PHP arrays are value types; a function
   wrapper would mutate a copy rather than the original.

name: assert
doc: Throws an exception if expr is falsy. Optional message string. Used for precondition checking in application code. When `*assert*` is logical false at macroexpansion time, `assert` expands to nil and performs no runtime check.

name: assert-non-nil-pair
doc:
Rejects `nil` operands so ordered comparisons fail loudly instead of silently coercing `nil` to 0. Mirrors the arithmetic functions, which already reject `nil`, and matches Clojure/JVM (which throws).

  Named `-pair` rather than `assert-non-nil`: `core/math` defines a variadic
  `assert-non-nil` in this same namespace and loads *after* `core/booleans`, so
  the short name resolved to the variadic one at runtime and these comparisons
  paid a rest-argument allocation on every call. The name has to differ for the
  fixed arity to survive.

name: assert-var!
doc: Throws `InvalidArgumentException` with `msg` unless `v` is a `Var`.

name: assoc
doc: Associates one or more key-value pairs with a collection. Additional key-value pairs beyond the first are applied in order. Throws if an odd number of extra arguments is provided.

name: assoc-in
doc:
Associates a value in a nested data structure at the given path.

Creates intermediate maps if they don't exist.

name: assoc-pair
doc: Associates a single key-value pair with a collection.

name: assoc!
doc:
Associates one or more key-value pairs with a transient collection,
   mutating it in place. Works on transient hash-maps and transient vectors.
   Variadic forms apply each `key-value` pair in order. A trailing key
   without a value is associated with `nil`. Raises
   `InvalidArgumentException` when `tcoll` is not a supported transient
   collection. Matches Clojure's `assoc!` semantics.

name: associative?
doc:
Returns true if `x` is an associative data structure, false otherwise.

  Associative data structures include vectors, hash maps, structs, and PHP arrays
  (both indexed and associative), matching Clojure's `Associative` protocol.

name: async
doc:
Runs body asynchronously in a new fiber. Returns an Amp\Future.

  Captures the caller's dynamic bindings and reinstalls them inside
  the fiber, so `binding`s established outside `async` are visible to
  `body` (binding conveyance, as in Clojure's `future`).

name: atom
doc:
Creates a new atom with the given value.

Atoms provide a way to manage mutable state. Use `reset!` to set a new value and `swap!` to update based on the current value.

Optional `:meta` and `:validator` keyword arguments may follow the value in any order. The validator is applied to the initial value when set.

name: atom?
doc: Returns true if the given value is an atom.

name: await
doc: Blocks the current fiber until the Future resolves and returns its value. Accepts either a raw `Amp\Future` or a `Future` wrapper.

name: await-all
doc: Awaits all Futures in the given collection. Returns a vector of results in the same order as the input collection, regardless of which Future resolves first. Accepts a mix of raw `Amp\Future` and `Future` wrappers.

name: await-any
doc: Awaits the first Future to resolve. Returns its value. Accepts a mix of raw `Amp\Future` and `Future` wrappers.

name: bean
doc: Returns a Phel map of the public properties of PHP object `obj`, with keyword keys. Inverse of `hydrate` for public-property objects.

name: bigdec
doc: Coerces `x` to a `Phel\Lang\BigDecimal`. Accepts `BigDecimal` (returned as-is), ints, floats (via the shortest round-trip decimal of the float), `BigInt`, `Ratio` (computed via exact decimal division; throws `ArithmeticError` when the expansion does not terminate, matching `(bigdec 1/3)`), and numeric strings.

name: bigdec?
doc: Returns true when `x` is a `Phel\Lang\BigDecimal` value.

name: bigint
doc:
Coerces `x` to a `Phel\Lang\BigInt`. Accepts ints, floats
  (truncated toward zero, rejecting `NaN`/`Inf`), numeric strings, and
  `BigInt` values.

name: bigint?
doc: Returns true when `x` is a `Phel\Lang\BigInt` value.

name: biginteger
doc: Alias for `bigint`. Coerces `x` to a `Phel\Lang\BigInt`.

name: binding
doc:
Temporarily rebinds dynamic vars while executing `body`.

  Each var in `bindings` must be tagged `^:dynamic` at its `def`. The
  rebinding is fiber-local: concurrent fibers observe independent
  values, and child futures (`future`, `async`, `future-fiber`)
  inherit the bindings active at their creation.

  Throws at runtime if any var in the bindings vector is not
  `:dynamic`. To swap a non-dynamic var for the duration of an
  expression (e.g. mocking in tests), use `with-redefs`.

name: bit-and
doc: Bitwise and.

name: bit-and-not
doc: Bitwise `and` with the complement of each subsequent argument: `(bit-and-not x y)` is `x & ~y`. Additional arguments are folded in left to right, clearing every bit that is set in any of them.

name: bit-clear
doc: Returns the integer `x` with the bit at index `n` (0-based, least significant first) cleared to 0.

name: bit-flip
doc: Returns the integer `x` with the bit at index `n` (0-based, least significant first) toggled.

name: bit-not
doc: Bitwise complement.

name: bit-or
doc: Bitwise or.

name: bit-set
doc: Returns the integer `x` with the bit at index `n` (0-based, least significant first) set to 1.

name: bit-shift-left
doc: Bitwise shift left.

name: bit-shift-right
doc: Bitwise shift right.

name: bit-test
doc: Returns `true` if the bit at index `n` (0-based, least significant first) of the integer `x` is set, `false` otherwise.

name: bit-xor
doc: Bitwise xor.

name: boolean
doc:
Coerces `x` to a boolean. Returns `false` if `x` is `nil` or `false`,
   `true` otherwise.

name: boolean?
doc: Returns true if `x` is a boolean, false otherwise.

name: bound?
doc: Returns true when `v` has a current root binding in the namespace registry. `v` must be a `Var`.

name: bounded-count
doc: Returns the number of items in `coll`, but counts at most `n` when `coll` is not `counted?`. If `coll` is `counted?` (its size is known in O(1)) the full `count` is returned, which may exceed `n`; otherwise the sequence is walked at most `n` steps.

name: butlast
doc:
Returns all but the last item in `coll`. Returns `nil` when `coll` is
  `nil` or has fewer than two items.

name: byte
doc: Coerces `x` to a signed 8-bit integer in the range `-128..127`. Decimal values are truncated toward zero. `Ratio` and `BigInt` values are accepted (truncate toward zero, then range-check). Values outside the range or non-numeric inputs raise `InvalidArgumentException`. Phel has no dedicated byte type, so the result is a plain PHP int.

name: canonical-ns
doc: Returns the canonical (dot-separated) form of a namespace string. Pass user-supplied namespace strings through this before any registry lookup or write.

name: case
doc: Evaluates expression and matches it against constant test values, returning the associated result.

name: cat
doc: A transducer that concatenates the contents of each input into the reduction.

name: ceil
doc: Returns the smallest integer not less than `x`. Ints and `BigInt` values are returned unchanged. Ratios collapse via ceiling division. Floats route through PHP's `ceil`.

name: char
doc: Coerces `x` to a single-character string representing the given Unicode code point. Accepts a non-negative integer (the code point, converted via `mb_chr`) or a single-character string, which is returned as-is. Phel has no dedicated char type — character literals such as `\A` are already single-character strings — so the result is always a plain string. Matches Clojure's `char` for `.cljc` interop; raises `InvalidArgumentException` on negative ints, non-single-character strings, and all other inputs.

name: char?
doc:
Returns true if `x` is a single-character string, false otherwise.
   Phel has no dedicated character type — character literals such as
   `\A` are already single-character strings — so `char?` is true for
   any string of length 1 (UTF-8 counted). Matches ClojureScript's
   `char?` for `.cljc` interop; Clojure/JVM's `char?` tests for the
   distinct `Character` type, which does not exist here.

name: clamp-int
doc:
Truncates a numeric `x` toward zero and range-checks it against `lo..hi`.
   Raises `InvalidArgumentException` when `x` is non-numeric or out of range.
   `label` names the target type for error messages.

name: class
doc: Returns a `Phel\Lang\PhpClass` for `x`. With an object argument returns the class of the object. With a string argument resolves the named class or interface FQN. Throws `InvalidArgumentException` for any other input.

name: class-name
doc: Returns the FQN string of `c` (a `Phel\Lang\PhpClass`). Leading backslashes are not preserved (e.g. `\stdClass` becomes `stdClass`).

name: class?
doc: Returns true if `x` is a `Phel\Lang\PhpClass` value.

name: close-resource
doc:
Close dispatch used by `with-open`: objects with a `close` method are
  closed via that method, stream resources via `php/fclose`. Nil and values
  without a known close strategy are skipped.

name: coerce-in
doc: Returns `v` if it is in the range, or `min` if `v` is less than `min`, or `max` if `v` is greater than `max`.

name: coll?
doc:
Returns true if `x` is a persistent collection — vector, list, hash-map
   (including sorted-map), struct, set (including sorted-set), or lazy-seq —
   and false otherwise. Strings, numbers, `nil`, booleans, keywords, symbols,
   and plain PHP arrays are not considered collections, matching Clojure's
   `IPersistentCollection` membership.

name: comment
doc: Ignores the body of the comment.

name: comp
doc: Takes a list of functions and returns a function that is the composition of those functions.

name: compact
doc: Returns a lazy sequence with specified values removed from `coll`. If no values are specified, removes nil values by default.

name: compare
doc:
Compares `x` and `y`, returning a negative
  integer, zero, or a positive integer when `x` is less than, equal to, or
  greater than `y`.

  `nil` is less than every non-nil value and equal to itself. Numbers are
  compared across the numeric tower (int, float, `Ratio`, `BigInt`,
  `BigDecimal`). Throws `InvalidArgumentException` when `x` and `y` come from
  mutually incomparable categories (e.g. `(compare 1 [])`).

name: compare-and-set!
doc: Atomically sets the value of the atom `variable` to `new-value` if and only if its current value is identical (via `identical?`) to `old-value`. Returns true when the swap happened, false otherwise.

name: compare-category
doc: Returns a coarse category for `compare`'s type compatibility check. `nil` is its own category so it can be treated as less than anything. Numbers share a category so `(compare 1 1.5)` works.

name: compare-to-zero
doc:
Returns the sign comparison of `x` against zero across the numeric tower
  (PHP int, BigInt, Ratio, float). Negative for x<0, 0 for x=0,
  positive for x>0.

name: compile
doc: Returns the compiled PHP code string for the given form.

name: complement
doc: Returns a function that takes the same arguments as `f` and returns the opposite truth value.

name: completing
doc: Takes a reducing function `f` of 2 args and returns a fn suitable for transduce by adding a 1-arity (completion) that calls `cf` (default: identity).

name: compute-ancestors
doc: Computes all transitive ancestors of tag from a parents map.

name: compute-ancestors-map
doc: Builds the full {tag #{ancestors}} map from a parents map.

name: compute-derive-ancestors
doc: Like `compute-ancestors` but only follows `derive`-recorded edges.

name: compute-descendants-map
doc: Builds the full {tag #{descendants}} map from a parents map. Walks only `derive`-recorded edges, mirroring `descendants`'s contract.

name: concat
doc: Concatenates multiple sequential data structures.

name: concat
doc: Concatenates multiple collections into a lazy sequence.

name: concat1
doc: Concatenates two sequential data structures.

name: cond
doc: Evaluates test/expression pairs, returning the first matching expression.
example: (cond (< x 0) "negative" (> x 0) "positive" "zero") ; => "negative", "positive", or "zero" depending on x

name: cond->
doc: Takes an expression and a set of test/form pairs. Threads `expr` (via `->`) through each form for which the corresponding test expression is true. Note that, unlike `cond` branching, `cond->` threading does not short-circuit after the first true test expression.

name: cond->>
doc: Takes an expression and a set of test/form pairs. Threads `expr` (via `->>`) through each form for which the corresponding test expression is true. Note that, unlike `cond` branching, `cond->>` threading does not short-circuit after the first true test expression.

name: condp
doc:
Takes a binary predicate, an expression, and a set of clauses.
  Each clause takes the form of either:
    test-expr result-expr
    test-expr :>> result-fn
  For each clause, (pred test-expr expr) is evaluated. If it returns
  logical true, the clause is a match. If a binary clause is a match,
  result-expr is returned. If a ternary clause with :>> is a match,
  the result of (pred test-expr expr) is passed to result-fn and the
  return value is the result. If no clause matches, the default value
  is returned (if provided), otherwise an exception is thrown.

name: conj
doc: Returns a new collection with values added. Appends to vectors/sets, prepends to lists.

name: conj!
doc: Adds `value` to the transient collection `tcoll`, mutating it in place, and returns `tcoll`. The 'addition' may happen at different 'places' depending on the concrete transient type: transient vectors append at the tail, transient hash-sets add the element (no-op if already present), and transient hash-maps treat `value` as a `[key value]` pair (or an associative collection of entries). With zero arguments returns a new empty transient vector. With one argument returns `tcoll` unchanged. Variadic forms reduce `conj!` over the remaining values. Raises `InvalidArgumentException` when `tcoll` is not a transient collection. Matches Clojure's `conj!` semantics.

name: cons
doc: Prepends an element to the beginning of a collection.

name: constantly
doc: Returns a function that always returns `x` and ignores any passed arguments.

name: contains-value?
doc: Returns true if the value is present in the given collection, otherwise returns false.

name: contains?
doc: Returns true if key is present in collection (checks keys/indices, not values).

name: copy-meta
doc: Returns `target` with the metadata from `source` when both implement `MetaInterface`.

name: core-munge-name
doc: Encodes a definition name for registry lookup.

name: core-munge-ns
doc: Encodes a namespace string for registry lookup.

name: count
doc:
Counts the number of elements in a sequence. Can be used on everything that implements the PHP Countable interface.

Works with lists, vectors, hash-maps, sets, strings, and PHP arrays. Returns 0 for nil.

Throws for a lazily consumed source that has no size of its own — a transducer pipeline built by `eduction`, a PHP generator, an iterator. Counting one means draining it, which re-runs the whole pipeline (including its side effects) and still leaves nothing counted behind, so `count` refuses instead of doing it silently. Realize it first: `(count (into [] coll))`.

name: counted?
doc:
Returns true if `coll` can report its length in constant time — persistent
   vectors, lists, hash-maps (including sorted-map), structs, and sets
   (including sorted-set). Returns false for lazy sequences (counting them
   requires realizing the whole sequence), strings, numbers, `nil`, and every
   other non-counted type. Matches Clojure's `counted?` semantics, which
   mirror the `clojure.lang.Counted` marker interface.

name: create-ns
doc: Creates the given namespace if it does not already exist. Returns the namespace name in display form. Existing namespaces are left untouched.

name: csv-seq
doc: Returns a lazy sequence of rows from a CSV file.

name: cycle
doc: Returns an infinite lazy sequence that cycles through the elements of collection. Maps are iterated as `[key value]` pairs.

name: dbg
doc: Prints `[file:line] form => value` to the standard error stream and returns the value unchanged, so it can wrap any subexpression without restructuring code. With no argument prints just `[file:line]` as a reached-here marker and returns nil.
example:
(defn area [w h] (* (dbg w) h))
(area 3 4) ; stderr: [src/main.phel:12] w => 3

name: dbg-write
doc: Writes `message` to the standard error stream. Output primitive behind the `dbg` macro; redefine it with `with-redefs` to capture debug output in tests.

name: dec
doc: Decrements `x` by one.

name: dec'
doc:
Auto-promoting variant of `dec`. Integer results are returned as
  `BigInt`; floats and rationals pass through unchanged.

name: decimal-string->rational
doc:
Parses a decimal or scientific-notation string into a Ratio
  (auto-collapsed to int / BigInt when integral).

name: decimal?
doc: Alias for `bigdec?`. Returns true when `x` is a `Phel\Lang\BigDecimal`.

name: declare
doc: Declare a global symbol before it is defined.

name: dedupe
doc: Returns a lazy sequence with consecutive duplicate values removed in `coll`. When called with no args, returns a transducer.

name: deep-merge
doc: Recursively merges data structures.

name: def-
doc: Define a private value that will not be exported.

name: defenum
doc:
Defines a native PHP enum. Each case is named by a keyword followed by an
  optional scalar value (all `int` or all `string`); value-less cases produce a
  pure enum. After the cases, an optional implementations tail (interface
  symbols with their methods, and a `:php` block of plain/magic methods) is
  parsed like `defstruct`, so an enum can implement interfaces and carry
  methods. Also defines a `Name?` predicate.

      (defenum Status :active "active" :inactive "inactive")
      (Status? Status/active) # => true

      (defenum Suit
        :hearts :spades :clubs :diamonds
        Describable
        (describe [this] (.-name this))
        :php
        (label [this] (.-name this)))

name: defexception
doc:
Define a new exception. Optionally pass a parent class to extend (defaults to
  `Exception`), so frameworks can catch it by type, e.g.
  `(defexception ProductNotFound RuntimeException)`. The parent takes any class
  spelling: bare, dotted (`My.Ns.Error`), or an alias brought in with `:use`.

name: definterface
doc: An interface in Phel defines an abstract set of functions. It is directly mapped to a PHP interface. An interface can be defined by using the definterface macro.

name: defmacro
doc: Define a macro.

name: defmacro-
doc: Define a private macro that will not be exported.

name: defmethod
doc:
Registers a method implementation for a multimethod.

  `multi-name` is the name of the multimethod defined by `defmulti`.
  When extending a multimethod from a different namespace, fully qualify
  the multi-name (e.g. `phel\test/assert-expr`) so the methods table is
  resolved in the multimethod's home namespace.
  `dispatch-val` is the value that triggers this method.
  `args` and `body` define the function implementation.

name: defmulti
doc:
Defines a multimethod. `dispatch-fn` is called on the arguments to
  produce a dispatch value, which is then used to select the appropriate
  method registered via `defmethod`.

  An optional docstring may be provided between `name` and `dispatch-fn`.

  If no method matches the dispatch value, the `:default` method is used
  (if defined), otherwise an error is thrown.

name: defn
doc: Define a new global function.

name: defn-
doc: Define a private function that will not be exported.

name: defprotocol
doc:
Defines a protocol with the given method signatures. Each method signature is a list of (method-name [args]).

Creates a dispatching function for each method that dispatches on the type of the first argument. Use `extend-type` to add implementations.

A `:default` type can be registered via `extend-type` as a fallback when no specific type implementation is found.

name: defrecord
doc:
Defines a record type with the given fields, matching Clojure's `defrecord`.

  Expands to a `defstruct` plus Clojure-style factory functions:
  - `Name` — positional constructor (from `defstruct`)
  - `Name?` — type predicate (from `defstruct`)
  - `->Name` — positional factory, identical to `Name`
  - `map->Name` — map factory that takes `{:field value ...}`

  An optional tail of protocol/method forms is spliced into an `extend-type`
  call, so inline protocol implementations work exactly like Clojure's
  `defrecord` body. Only Phel protocols are supported in the inline tail;
  PHP interface implementations remain on `defstruct`.

name: defs->map
doc:
Builds a {decoded-name => value} map of the definitions in `encoded-ns`,
  keeping only those whose encoded `fn-name` satisfies `keep?`.

name: defstruct
doc: A Struct is a special kind of Map. It only supports a predefined number of keys and is associated to a global name. The Struct not only defines itself but also a predicate function.

name: deftype
doc:
Defines a type with the given fields, matching Clojure's `deftype` syntax.

  Expands to a `defstruct` plus a Clojure-style positional factory:
  - `Name` — positional constructor (from `defstruct`)
  - `Name?` — type predicate (from `defstruct`)
  - `->Name` — positional factory, identical to `Name`

  Unlike `defrecord`, no `map->Name` factory is generated.

  An optional tail of protocol/method forms is spliced into an `extend-type`
  call. Only Phel protocols are supported in the inline tail.

  Deviation from Clojure: Phel's `deftype` shares the map-backed
  `defstruct` infrastructure, so instances remain map-like (keys are
  accessible via `get`). Clojure's `deftype` produces a non-map type;
  if you need that semantic, use native PHP interop.

name: delay
doc: Takes a body of expressions and yields a Delay object that will invoke the body only the first time it is forced (via force or deref/@), caching the result.

name: delay?
doc: Returns true if x is a Delay.

name: deliver
doc: Delivers `value` to `p` if it is still unrealized. Returns `p` on first delivery, `nil` if `p` was already delivered.

name: denominator
doc: Returns the denominator of `r`. For rationals the denominator collapses to a PHP int when it fits; integers and `BigInt` values report `1`.

name: deref
doc:
Returns the current value inside an atom or var.

For atoms returns the current cell value; for `Var` instances returns the current root binding from the namespace registry.

With three arguments, and when `variable` is a future or promise, blocks for at most `timeout-ms` milliseconds waiting for it to resolve. If the awaitable has not completed within the timeout, returns `timeout-val`.

name: derive
doc: Establishes a parent/child relationship between child and parent keywords. With two arguments, mutates the global hierarchy and returns nil. With a hierarchy `h`, returns a new hierarchy with the relationship added; the original hierarchy is not modified. Throws on cyclic derivation.

name: derive-only-parents
doc: Returns parents recorded by `derive` for tag, ignoring PHP class inheritance and protocol relations. Used by `descendants` to match Clojure's contract that type inheritance is not surfaced.

name: descendants
doc:
Returns the set of all descendants of tag, or nil.
  Only `derive`-recorded relationships are walked: type inheritance
  (PHP class hierarchy, protocol extensions) is not surfaced, matching
  Clojure's contract.

name: difference
doc: Difference between multiple sets into a new one.

name: direct-parents
doc:
Returns manually-derived parents plus PHP type parents for tag.

  Layers `derive`-recorded edges with PHP class inheritance and the
  protocol-implementor registry so `parents`/`ancestors` surface every
  relationship. `descendants` (which must ignore type inheritance) uses
  `derive-only-parents` directly.

name: disj
doc: Returns a new set that does not contain the given key(s). Works on hash-sets and sorted-sets. Removing a non-existent key is a no-op. Returns `nil` when called on `nil`.

name: disj!
doc: Removes one or more elements from a transient set, mutating it in place. Raises `InvalidArgumentException` when `tcoll` is not a transient set. Matches Clojure's `disj!` semantics.

name: display-ns
doc: Returns the display (dot-separated) form of a namespace string. Equivalent to `canonical-ns`; kept as a separate name so call sites read intent (display vs. canonicalize).

name: dissoc
doc: Returns `ds` without the given keys. With no keys returns `ds` unchanged.

name: dissoc-in
doc: Dissociates a value from a nested data structure at the given path.

name: dissoc!
doc: Dissociates one or more keys from a transient map, mutating it in place. Raises `InvalidArgumentException` when `tcoll` is not a transient map. Matches Clojure's `dissoc!` semantics.

name: distinct
doc: Returns a lazy sequence with duplicated values removed in `coll`. When called with no args, returns a transducer.

name: distinct?
doc: Returns true if no two of the arguments are `=`. Requires at least one argument.

name: doall
doc: Forces realization of a lazy sequence and returns it as a vector.

name: dofor
doc: Repeatedly executes body for side effects with bindings and modifiers as provided by for. Returns nil.

name: dominates?
doc: Returns true when candidate `x` is more specific than `y` for multimethod dispatch: either `x` derives from `y` in the hierarchy, or `x` is preferred over `y` via `prefer-method`.

name: dorun
doc: Forces realization of a lazy sequence for side effects, returns nil.

name: doseq
doc:
Repeatedly executes body for side effects with Clojure-style bindings.
  `(doseq [x coll] body)` runs `body` once per element of `coll`. When `coll`
  is a map, each iteration sees a `[k v]` entry pair, so destructuring works
  just like in Clojure: `(doseq [[k v] m] ...)`. Supports `:when`, `:while`,
  and `:let` modifiers between bindings.

name: doseq-iterable
doc:
Internal helper used by the `doseq` macro expansion. Returns a value
  suitable for Clojure-style iteration: maps are expanded to a sequence of
  `[k v]` pair vectors so destructuring binds entries as in Clojure. Every
  other value is returned unchanged.

name: doseq-normalize
doc: Transforms Clojure-style doseq bindings into Phel dofor format. Pairs `[x coll]` become triples `[x :in (doseq-iterable coll)]` so maps iterate as entry pairs. Already-present verb triples `[x :in coll]` pass through unchanged. Modifier keywords like `:when`, `:while`, `:let` pass through unchanged.

name: dotimes
doc: Evaluates body `n` times with `binding` bound to integers from 0 to n-1. Returns nil.

name: doto
doc: Evaluates x then calls all of the methods and functions with the value of x supplied at the front of the given arguments. The forms are evaluated in order. Returns x.

name: double
doc: Coerces `x` to a double. In PHP there is no distinction between float and double; both map to the same native PHP float type. Alias for `float`.

name: double-array
doc: Creates a PHP array of doubles (same as float-array in PHP). Accepts the same arities and semantics as `float-array`.

name: double?
doc: Returns true if `x` is a floating-point number, false otherwise. Alias for `float?`, matching Clojure's `double?` naming. Since Phel uses PHP floats (IEEE 754 doubles) there is no separate single-precision float type.

name: drop
doc: Drops the first `n` elements of `coll`. Returns a lazy sequence. When called with n only, returns a transducer.

name: drop-last
doc: Drops the last `n` elements of `coll`. `n` defaults to `1` when omitted, matching Clojure's `(drop-last coll)` single-arity form. Returns an empty sequence when `coll` is `nil`. Works with any seqable collection including lazy sequences and ranges.

name: drop-while
doc: Drops all elements at the front of `coll` where `(pred x)` is true. Returns a lazy sequence. When called with pred only, returns a transducer.

name: eduction
doc:
Returns a reducible/iterable applying transducers to `coll`. The last
  argument is the source collection; preceding arguments are transducers
  composed left-to-right. The transformation is re-run on each consumption
  (no caching), so the result is safe to reduce or iterate multiple times.

name: emit-binding-form
doc:
Builds the open/try/commit/finally skeleton shared by `binding` and
  `with-redefs`. `open-method` is the `\Phel` static used to start the
  fiber-local recording (`openBindingFrame` for dynamic-only,
  `openRedefsFrame` for any var).

name: emit-set-vars
doc:
Expands a `[v1 e1 v2 e2 ...]` binding vector into the sequence of
  `(set-var v e)` forms consumed by an open binding/with-redefs frame.

name: empty
doc: Returns an empty collection of the same category as `coll`, preserving the original metadata, or nil if `coll` has no empty equivalent.

name: empty?
doc:
Returns true if x would be 0, "" or empty collection, false otherwise. Safe on infinite/lazy sequences: checks the first element instead of counting.

A non-countable iterable (an `eduction` pipeline, a PHP generator) is answered by pulling a single element, never by counting it.

name: ensure-php-array
doc:
Returns `arr` when it is a PHP array, otherwise throws an
  `InvalidArgumentException` naming the calling operation.

name: ensure-reduced
doc: Wraps `x` in Reduced if it is not already reduced.

name: eval
doc: Evaluates a form and return the evaluated results.

name: even?
doc: Checks if `x` is even.

name: every-pred
doc: Takes a variadic set of predicates and returns a function `f` that, when called with any number of arguments, returns `true` if every composing predicate returns a logical true value against every argument, and `false` otherwise. The returned function short-circuits on the first logical false result: arguments after it are not inspected, and predicates after it are not tried. Predicates are consulted in the order supplied; for a given predicate, arguments are consulted left-to-right. With no arguments the returned function returns `true`.
example:
((every-pred even? pos?) 2 4 6) ; => true
((every-pred even? pos?) 2 -4) ; => false

name: every?
doc: Returns true if predicate is true for every element in collection, false otherwise. Alias for `all?`.

name: ex-cause
doc: Returns the cause of an exception, or nil.

name: ex-data
doc: Returns the data map from an ex-info exception, or nil if not an ExceptionInfo.

name: ex-info
doc: Creates an exception with a message and a data map. Optionally takes a cause.

name: ex-message
doc: Returns the message of an exception.

name: extend-protocol
doc:
Convenience macro that extends a single protocol to multiple types. Alternates type-specs and method implementations.

Equivalent to multiple `extend-type` calls.

name: extend-type
doc:
Extends a type with protocol method implementations.

  type-spec can be:
  - `nil` for the nil type
  - a type keyword matching what `type` returns: `:string`, `:int`, `:float`,
    `:boolean`, `:keyword`, `:symbol`, `:vector`, `:list`, `:hash-map`, `:set`,
    `:atom`, `:var`, `:function`, `:php/array`
  - a symbol for struct names (resolved in current namespace)
  - a string for explicit PHP class names (cross-namespace structs)

  Note: `:struct` and `:php/object` cannot be used as type-specs because
  protocol dispatch resolves these to their specific PHP class names.
  Use a struct symbol or PHP class name string instead.

name: extends?
doc: Returns true if the given type-key has implementations for all methods of the protocol. type-key should match what protocol-type-key returns.

name: extreme
doc: Returns the most extreme value in `args` based on the binary `order` function.

name: false?
doc: Checks if value is exactly false (not just falsy).

name: ffirst
doc: Same as `(first (first coll))`.

name: fiber-facade
doc: Lazily resolves the shared FiberFacade instance.

name: file-get-contents-silenced
doc: Wrapper around file_get_contents that suppresses PHP warnings. We handle errors by checking the return value.

name: file-seq
doc: Returns a lazy sequence of all files and directories in a directory tree.

name: filter
doc: Returns a lazy sequence of elements where predicate returns true. When called with pred only, returns a transducer.

name: filterv
doc: Returns a vector of the items in `coll` for which `(pred item)` returns a logical true value. Like `filter`, but eager and returns a vector rather than a lazy sequence.

name: find
doc: When called with a collection first, returns `[key value]` when `key` is present. Otherwise returns the first item in `coll` where `(pred item)` evaluates to true.

name: find-hierarchy-method
doc:
Finds the best matching method for dispatch-val using the global hierarchy.
  Returns the method function or nil. Used internally by defmulti. When
  multiple methods match and none is more specific, consults `prefers-map`
  (built by `prefer-method`); if still ambiguous, throws.

name: find-index
doc: Returns the index of the first item in `coll` where `(pred item)` evaluates to true.

name: find-ns
doc: Returns the namespace name in display form if it is loaded, or nil if no namespace of that name exists. Accepts dot or backslash separators on input.

name: find-var
doc: Returns the `Var` named by the fully-qualified symbol, or nil if no matching definition exists. Tries the symbol name verbatim first (matching how `def` stores entries), then falls back to the encoded form (matching how `intern` stores entries).

name: first
doc:
Returns the first element of a sequence, or nil if empty.

Maps are treated as a sequence of entries: `(first {:a 1})` returns a typed `MapEntry` equal by value to `[:a 1]`. Strings are treated as sequences of multibyte characters.

A lazily consumed source with no indexed access of its own (an `eduction` pipeline, a PHP generator, an iterator) is answered by pulling a single element, the same way `empty?` answers it. `count` is the one that refuses such a source, because counting means draining it.

name: first-map-entry
doc: Returns the first entry of a persistent map as a typed `MapEntry`, or nil if empty.

name: first-of-set
doc: Returns the first value of a persistent set, or nil if empty.

name: first-of-string
doc: Returns the first multibyte character of a string, or nil if empty.

name: flatten
doc: Flattens nested sequential structure into a lazy sequence of all leaf values.

name: float
doc:
Coerces `x` to a float. In PHP there is no distinction between float and
   double; both map to the same native PHP float type. `Ratio`,
   `BigInt`, and `BigDecimal` values collapse to their float value;
   everything else delegates to PHP's `floatval`, so non-numeric strings
   return `0.0` and `nil` returns `0.0`. Non-numeric objects such as
   keywords, vectors, or maps raise `InvalidArgumentException` instead of
   leaking a raw PHP float-coercion warning.

name: float->rational
doc: Converts a finite float to a Ratio using its shortest round-trip decimal expansion. Non-finite floats are rejected.

name: float-array
doc: Creates a PHP array of floats. Accepts the same arities as `int-array`; coerces elements to float via `floatval` and zero-pads with `0.0`.

name: float-shortest-decimal
doc: Shortest %g-formatted decimal that round-trips back to `x`. Tries increasing precision so 0.1 becomes "0.1", not "0.10000000000000001".

name: float-to-str
doc: Renders a float so integer-valued floats keep the trailing `.0`, while `NaN` and ±Infinity stringify readably.

name: float?
doc: Returns true if `x` is float point number, false otherwise.

name: floor
doc: Returns the largest integer not greater than `x`. Ints and `BigInt` values are returned unchanged. Ratios collapse via floor division. Floats route through PHP's `floor`.

name: fn?
doc: Returns true if `x` is a function, false otherwise.

name: fnext
doc: Same as `(first (next coll))`.

name: fnil
doc: Returns a function that replaces nil arguments with the provided defaults before calling f. The number of defaults determines how many leading arguments are nil-checked.

name: for
doc:
List comprehension. The head of the loop is a vector that contains a
  sequence of bindings modifiers and options. A binding is a sequence of three
  values `binding :verb expr`. Where `binding` is a binding as
  in let and `:verb` is one of the following keywords:

  * `:range` loop over a range by using the range function.
  * `:in` loops over all values of a collection (including strings).
  * `:keys` loops over all keys/indexes of a collection.
  * `:pairs` loops over all key-value pairs of a collection.

  After each loop binding, additional modifiers can be applied. Modifiers
  have the form `:modifier argument`. The following modifiers are supported:

  * `:while` breaks the loop if the expression is falsy.
  * `:let` defines additional bindings.
  * `:when` only evaluates the loop body if the condition is true.

  Finally, additional options can be set:

  * `:reduce [accumulator initial-value]` Instead of returning a list,
     it reduces the values into `accumulator`. Initially `accumulator`
     is bound to `initial-value`.

name: for-verb?
doc: True when `x` is one of the keywords accepted by `for` / `dofor` as a verb.

name: force
doc: If x is a Delay, forces it and returns its cached value. Otherwise returns x.

name: format
doc: Returns a formatted string. See PHP's [sprintf](https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.sprintf.php) for more information.

name: frequencies
doc:
Returns a map from distinct items in `coll` to the number of times they appear.

Works with vectors, lists, sets, and strings.

name: full-name
doc: Return the namespace and name string of a string, keyword or symbol.

name: future
doc:
Starts evaluating `body` asynchronously and returns a `Future` that can be `deref`ed (blocks the current fiber until the value is available) or checked with `realized?`.

Supports the 3-arg `(deref f timeout-ms timeout-val)` form for time-bounded blocking, as well as `future-cancel`, `future-cancelled?` and `future-done?` for lifecycle management.

Must be called from inside a fiber context (e.g. the AMPHP event loop or an enclosing `async` block), because `deref` resolves via AMPHP's fiber-based `await`.

name: future-call
doc:
Invokes `f` (a zero-arg function) in a new fiber. Returns a
  `PhelFiberFuture` you can `deref` or inspect with `future-done?`
  and `future-cancel`.

  Captures the caller's dynamic bindings and reinstalls them inside
  the fiber before invoking `f`, so bindings are conveyed the same
  way as with `future`/`async`.

name: future-cancel
doc: Signals the future's internal cancellation token, causing any pending or subsequent `deref` call to raise `CancelledException` (or return the timeout value for the 3-arg form). Due to AMPHP's cooperative fibers, the body keeps running until its next cancellation checkpoint; from the caller's perspective the future behaves as cancelled after this returns.

name: future-cancelled?
doc: Returns `true` if `future-cancel` was called on `f`, `false` otherwise.

name: future-done?
doc:
Returns `true` if the future is in a final state (completed, failed, or cancelled).

Dispatches on type: for a `Phel.Fiber.Domain.Future` (fiber-backed) it calls `isDone`; for any other value it falls back to `realized?`. This lets the same predicate serve both the AMPHP `Future` wrapper and the cooperative fiber future.

name: future-fiber
doc:
Runs `body` in a new fiber via the cooperative scheduler. Returns a
  fiber-future that supports `deref`, `realized?`, `future-done?`, and
  `future-cancel`. Works at the top level (no enclosing `async` block
  required), in contrast to `future` which requires an AMPHP fiber
  context.

name: future?
doc: Returns true if `x` is a fiber-future (from `future-call`/`future-fiber`) or a `Future` (from the AMPHP-backed `future` macro).

name: gcd
doc:
Returns the greatest common divisor of `a` and `b`, computed with the
  Euclidean algorithm. The result is always non-negative; `(gcd 0 0)` is `0`.

name: gensym
doc: Generates a new unique symbol.

name: get
doc: Gets the value at key in a collection. Returns default if not found.

name: get-in
doc:
Accesses a value in a nested data structure via a sequence of keys.

Returns `opt` (default nil) when a key is missing mid-traversal. When the path is nil or empty, returns `ds` as-is (which may be nil).

name: get-validator
doc: Returns the validator function of a variable, or nil.

name: group-by
doc: Returns a map of the elements of coll keyed by the result of `f` on each element.

name: group-protocol-specs
doc:
Splits a flat protocol spec list into `[[header [methods]] ...]` groups.
  A spec for which `(header? spec)` is truthy starts a new group; every other
  spec is a method appended to the current group. Used by `extend-type`,
  `extend-protocol`, and `reify`, which differ only in the header predicate.

name: hash-map
doc: Creates a new hash map. If no argument is provided, an empty hash map is created. The number of parameters must be even. Shortcut: {}

name: hash-set
doc: Creates a new Set from the given arguments. Shortcut: #{}

name: hierarchy-tag
doc: Resolves public type constructor functions to their generated PHP class tag.

name: hydrate
doc: Creates an instance of PHP class `class-name` (a class-string) without invoking its constructor, then sets each declared property named by the keyword keys of map `m`. Mirrors how ORMs/serializers rebuild entities from raw data; pairs with `bean` for the reverse direction.

name: ident?
doc: Returns true if `x` is a symbol or keyword.

name: identical?
doc: Checks if all values are identical. Same as `a === b` in PHP.

name: identity
doc: Returns its argument.

name: if-let
doc: If test is true, evaluates then with binding-form bound to the value of test, if not, yields else

name: if-not
doc: Evaluates then if test is false, else otherwise.

name: if-some
doc: Binds name to the value of test. If test is not nil, evaluates then with binding-form bound to the value of test, if not, yields else. Unlike if-let, false and 0 are not treated as falsy — only nil triggers the else branch.

name: ifn?
doc: Returns true if `x` can be invoked as a function. This includes functions, keywords, maps, vectors, sets, and lists.

name: inc
doc: Increments `x` by one.

name: inc'
doc:
Auto-promoting variant of `inc`. Integer results are returned as
  `BigInt`; floats and rationals pass through unchanged.

name: index
doc: Returns a map that groups the maps in the relation `xrel` by their values for the keys in `ks`. Each key is `(select-keys map ks)` and each value is the set of maps sharing those key-values.

name: indexed?
doc:
Returns true if `x` is an indexed sequence, false otherwise.

Indexed sequences include lists, vectors, and indexed PHP arrays.

name: inf?
doc: Checks if `x` is infinite.

name: infinite?
doc: Checks if `x` is positive or negative infinity. Alias for `inf?`, matching Clojure's `infinite?` naming.

name: instance?
doc:
Returns true if `x` is an instance of class `c`, false otherwise.
  Mirrors Clojure's `clojure.core/instance?` argument order (class first,
  value second). `c` should be a literal class reference such as
  `DateTime` or a `:use`d short name; for runtime class names use
  `(php/is_a x class-name)`.

name: int
doc:
Coerces `x` to an integer. `Ratio` and `BigDecimal` values truncate
   toward zero (`(int 1/10)` is `0`, `(int -1.1M)` is `-1`); `BigInt`
   and `float` values collapse to their PHP int value or throw
   `OverflowException` when outside the PHP int range (`NaN`/`Inf` floats
   raise `InvalidArgumentException`). Numeric strings are parsed via PHP's
   `intval`, and `nil` returns `0`. Non-numeric objects such as keywords,
   vectors, or maps raise `InvalidArgumentException` instead of leaking a
   raw PHP int-coercion warning.

name: int-array
doc:
Creates a PHP array of integers, matching Clojure's `clojure.core/int-array`.

  - `(int-array size-or-seq)` — given a non-negative integer, fills with `0`;
    given a sequence, coerces each element to int via `intval`.
  - `(int-array size init-val-or-seq)` — when `init-val-or-seq` is a number, every
    slot is filled with it (coerced to int). When it is a sequence, its elements
    fill the prefix of the array (truncated to `size` if longer) and the remaining
    slots are zero-padded.

  PHP has no typed arrays, so the result is a plain PHP array.

name: int?
doc: Returns true if `x` is a fixed-precision PHP integer. `BigInt` values return false; use `integer?` to accept either.

name: integer?
doc:
Returns true if `x` is a mathematical integer: a fixed-precision PHP
   `int` or a `BigInt`.

name: interleave
doc: Returns a lazy sequence of the first item in each `colls`, then the second item in each, until any one of the collections is exhausted. Any remaining items in the other collections are ignored. Returns an empty sequence when no collections are supplied or when any collection is empty or `nil`. Maps are iterated as `[key value]` pairs.

name: intern
doc: Finds or creates a definition named by name-str in namespace ns-str. When a value is supplied, sets the root value to val (overwriting any existing value). When no value is supplied, returns the existing definition unchanged, or creates a new one with nil if none exists. Auto-registers the namespace when creating a new definition; the arity-2 form is a no-op when the definition already exists. Returns the fully qualified symbol naming the definition (with the namespace in display form).

name: interpose
doc: Returns elements separated by a separator. Returns a lazy sequence. When called with sep only, returns a transducer.

name: intersection
doc: Intersect multiple sets into a new one.

name: into
doc:
Returns `to` with all elements of `from` added.

When `from` is associative, it is treated as a sequence of key-value pairs. Supports persistent and transient collections.

name: into-array
doc:
Returns a PHP array containing the elements of `aseq`. Accepts any
  collection (vector, list, set, map, PHP array) or `nil`, which yields
  an empty PHP array. The optional `type` argument is accepted for
  `.cljc` interop but has no runtime effect — PHP has no typed arrays,
  so the result is always a plain PHP array. Use the dedicated coercion
  helpers (`int-array`, `long-array`, `float-array`, `double-array`,
  `short-array`) when element coercion is actually required.

name: invert
doc:
Returns a new map where the keys and values are swapped.

If map has duplicated values, some keys will be ignored.

name: invoke-target-name
doc:
Returns the name to report for `target` in an undefined-method error:
  the class of an object, the string itself for a class name, and the PHP
  type for anything else.

name: isa-in?
doc: Checks if child is (transitively) a descendant of parent in parents-map. Walks up the parent chain without building the full ancestor set.

name: isa?
doc: Returns true if child equals parent, or child is a descendant of parent. When a hierarchy is provided, the check is performed against it; otherwise the global hierarchy is used.

name: iterate
doc: Returns an infinite lazy sequence of x, (f x), (f (f x)), and so on.

name: iteration
doc:
Creates a lazy sequence from successive calls to `step`.
  `step` is called with a key (starting with `:initk`) and returns a result.
  `:kf` extracts the next key, `:vf` extracts the value from the result.
  Terminates when the result is nil.

  Options map keys:
    :kf     — key function (default: identity)
    :vf     — value function (default: identity)
    :initk  — initial key (default: nil)

name: iterator-seq
doc: Returns a lazy sequence over a PHP `Traversable` (Iterator, Generator, IteratorAggregate, ...), pulling one element at a time. Unlike the eager coercion that materialises a `Traversable` via `iterator_to_array`, this streams a large or infinite source (DB cursor, stream reader, paginated API), so `take`/`map`/`filter` only pull what they consume.

name: juxt
doc: Takes a list of functions and returns a new function that is the juxtaposition of those functions.

name: keep
doc: Returns a lazy sequence of non-nil results of applying function to elements. When called with f only, returns a transducer.

name: keep-indexed
doc: Returns a lazy sequence of non-nil results of `(pred i x)`. When called with f only, returns a transducer.

name: key
doc:
Returns the key of a map entry. Accepts a typed
  `Phel\Lang\Collections\Map\MapEntry` value or a 2-element vector
  `[key value]` (the form Phel maps yield when iterated).

name: keys
doc: Returns a sequence of all keys in a map, or `nil` when the map is `nil` or empty.

name: keyword
doc:
Creates a new Keyword.

  Arity-1 accepts a string, keyword, or symbol. Returns `nil` when `x` is `nil`.
  If `x` is already a keyword, it is returned unchanged. A string is split on
  the first `/` into namespace and name parts, like `symbol`.

  Arity-2 builds a namespaced keyword from the namespace and name parts (taken
  verbatim, without splitting); returns `nil` when `name` is `nil`. Non-string
  parts are converted with PHP's `strval` rather than `str`, which is both
  faster on this hot path and renders `true` as `"1"` and `false` as `""`.

name: keyword?
doc: Returns true if `x` is a keyword, false otherwise.

name: kvs
doc: Returns a vector of key-value pairs like `[k1 v1 k2 v2 k3 v3 ...]`.

name: last
doc: Returns the last element of `coll` or nil if `coll` is empty or nil.

name: lazy-cat
doc: Concatenates collections into a lazy sequence (expands to concat).

name: lazy-seq
doc: Creates a lazy sequence that evaluates the body only when accessed.

name: lazy-seq-from-generator
doc: Wraps a PHP Generator in a ChunkedSeq for efficient lazy evaluation. ChunkedSeq realizes elements in batches for better performance.

name: lazy-seq?
doc:
Returns true if `x` is a lazy sequence, false otherwise.

Unlike `seq?`, this predicate is true only for lazy sequences, not for realized lists. Use `seq?` if you want to accept either.

name: lcm
doc:
Returns the least common multiple of `a` and `b`. The result is always
  non-negative; when either argument is zero the result is `0`.

name: letfn
doc:
Defines mutually recursive local functions.

bindings is a vector of function specs: (letfn [(f [params] body) (g [params] body)] expr) All function names are in scope within all function bodies and the body expression, enabling mutual recursion.
example:
(letfn [(my-even? [n] (if (zero? n) true (my-odd? (dec n))))
        (my-odd? [n] (if (zero? n) false (my-even? (dec n))))]
  (my-even? 10))

name: line-seq
doc: Returns a lazy sequence of lines from a file.

name: list
doc: Creates a new list. If no argument is provided, an empty list is created. Shortcut: '()

name: list?
doc: Returns true if `x` is a list, false otherwise. Returns false for the seq view of non-list collections produced by `seq`.

name: load-file
doc: Loads and evaluates a Phel source file. Reads the file content and evaluates it using the compiler. Returns the result of the last expression, or nil if the file cannot be read.

name: loaded-namespaces
doc: Returns all namespaces currently loaded, in dot-separated display form.

name: long
doc: Coerces `x` to a long integer. In PHP there is no distinction between int and long; both map to the same native PHP int type. Alias for `int`.

name: long-array
doc: Creates a PHP array of longs (same as int-array in PHP). Accepts the same arities and semantics as `int-array`.

name: macroexpand
doc: Recursively expands the given form until it is no longer a macro call.

name: macroexpand-1
doc: Expands the given form once if it is a macro call.

name: make-hierarchy
doc:
Creates a fresh, empty hierarchy.

Returns a map with `:parents`, `:descendants`, and `:ancestors` keys, each holding an empty map. Matches Clojure's hierarchy shape so consumers can destructure any of the three relationship views.

name: map
doc:
Returns a lazy sequence of the result of applying `f` to all of the first items in each coll,
   followed by applying `f` to all the second items in each coll until anyone of the colls is exhausted.

  When given a single collection, applies the function to each element.
  When applied to a map, iterates over entries as `[key value]` pairs,
  matching Clojure semantics.
  With multiple collections, applies the function to corresponding elements from each collection,
  stopping when the shortest collection is exhausted.

name: map-entry
doc: Returns a typed `Phel\Lang\Collections\Map\MapEntry` for `k`/`v`. Equal to the two-element vector `[k v]` so existing code that destructures `[k v]` keeps working.

name: map-entry?
doc:
Returns true if `x` is a map entry. Accepts both the typed
  `Phel\Lang\Collections\Map\MapEntry` value and any 2-element vector
  (Phel maps still yield vectors when iterated).

name: map-indexed
doc:
