Maps a function over a collection with index. Returns a lazy sequence.

Applies `f` to each element in `xs`. `f` is a two-argument function where the first argument is the index (0-based) and the second is the element itself. Works with infinite sequences.

name: map-invert
doc: Returns a map with the keys and values of `m` swapped. When several keys share a value, the one visited last in iteration order wins.

name: map?
doc: Returns true if `x` is a hash map, false otherwise.

name: mapcat
doc:
Maps a function over one or more collections and concatenates the results.
  Returns a lazy sequence. When called with `f` alone, returns a transducer.

  With a single collection behaves like `(apply concat (map f coll))`. With
  multiple collections, `f` is called with corresponding elements from each
  (stopping when the shortest is exhausted) and the resulting sequences are
  concatenated.

name: mapv
doc: Returns a vector consisting of the result of applying `f` to the set of first items of each coll, followed by applying `f` to the set of second items in each coll, until any one of the colls is exhausted. Like `map`, but eager and returns a vector rather than a lazy sequence.

name: max
doc: Returns the maximum of all arguments. Returns `##NaN` whenever any numeric argument is `##NaN`.

name: max-key
doc: Returns the arg for which (k arg) is largest. On ties, returns the latest argument.

name: mean
doc: Returns the mean of `xs` as a float.

name: median
doc: Returns the median of `xs`. With an even-sized collection the result is the float average of the two middle elements.

name: memoize
doc: Returns a memoized version of the function `f`. The memoized function caches the return value for each set of arguments.

name: memoize-lru
doc:
Returns a memoized version of the function `f` with an LRU (Least Recently Used) cache limited to `max-size` entries. When the cache exceeds `max-size`, the least recently used entry is evicted. This prevents unbounded memory growth in long-running processes.

Without arguments, uses a default cache size of 128 entries.

name: merge
doc:
Merges multiple maps into one new map.

If a key appears in more than one collection, later values replace previous ones.

name: merge-with
doc: Merges multiple maps into one new map. If a key appears in more than one collection, the result of `(f current-val next-val)` is used.

name: meta
doc: Gets the metadata attached to a value. For a quoted symbol (`(meta 'foo)`) the definition metadata registered via `def` is returned. For any other expression the value is looked up at runtime and its `MetaInterface` metadata returned.

name: min
doc: Returns the minimum of all arguments. Returns `##NaN` whenever any numeric argument is `##NaN`.

name: min-key
doc: Returns the arg for which (k arg) is smallest. On ties, returns the latest argument.

name: mod
doc:
Returns the floor remainder of `dividend` / `divisor`. The result has
  the same sign as `divisor`. Differs from `rem` on mixed-sign operands:
  `(mod -7 3) => 2` while `(rem -7 3) => -1`.

name: name
doc: Returns the name string of a string, keyword or symbol.

name: namespace
doc: Return the namespace string of a symbol or keyword. Nil if not present.

name: namespaced-ident?
doc: Returns true when x is a keyword or symbol with a namespace.

name: NAN
doc: Constant for Not a Number (NAN) values.

name: nan?
doc: Checks if `x` is not a number.

name: NaN?
doc: Checks if `x` is not a number. Alias for `nan?`, matching Clojure's `NaN?`.

name: nat-int?
doc: Returns true if `x` is a non-negative integer (zero or positive). Accepts both fixed-precision PHP `int` and arbitrary-precision `BigInt` values.

name: neg-int?
doc: Returns true if `x` is a negative integer. Accepts both fixed-precision PHP `int` and arbitrary-precision `BigInt` values.

name: neg?
doc: Checks if `x` is smaller than zero.

name: next
doc: Returns the sequence after the first element, or nil if empty.

name: next-of-map
doc: Returns all entries after the first persistent map entry as `MapEntry` instances, or nil.

name: next-of-set
doc: Returns all values after the first persistent set value, or nil.

name: next-vector-or-nil
doc: Returns all values after the first array value as a persistent vector, or nil.

name: nfirst
doc: Same as `(next (first coll))`.

name: nil?
doc: Returns true if value is nil, false otherwise.

name: nnext
doc: Same as `(next (next coll))`.

name: not
doc: Returns true if value is falsy (nil or false), false otherwise.

name: not-any?
doc: Returns true if `(pred x)` is logical false for every `x` in `coll` or if `coll` is empty. Otherwise returns false.

name: not-empty
doc: Returns `coll` if it contains elements, otherwise nil.

name: not-every?
doc: Returns false if `(pred x)` is logical true for every `x` in collection `coll` or if `coll` is empty. Otherwise returns true.

name: not=
doc: Checks if all values are unequal. Same as `a != b` in PHP.

name: ns-aliases
doc:
Returns a hash-map of {alias => namespace} for all require aliases in the
  given namespace string. Target namespaces are returned in display form.

name: ns-interns
doc:
Returns a hash-map of {name => value} for every definition in the
  given namespace, including private ones. Returns an empty map if the
  namespace has no definitions.

name: ns-publics
doc:
Returns a hash-map of {name => value} for all public definitions in the
  given namespace string. Private definitions are excluded.

name: ns-refers
doc:
Returns a hash-map of {name => source-namespace} for all referred symbols
  in the given namespace string. Source namespaces are returned in display form.

name: nth
doc:
Returns the value at `index` in `coll`. Throws an
   OutOfBoundsException if the index is out of range and no
   `not-found` value is supplied. For indexed collections (vectors,
   strings) this is O(1); for sequences it is O(n).

name: nthnext
doc: Returns the nth next of `coll`, `(seq coll)` when `n` is 0. Returns nil if there are fewer than `n` elements remaining.

name: nthrest
doc: Returns the nth rest of `coll`, `coll` when `n` is less than 1. Returns an empty list once the collection is exhausted.

name: number?
doc: Returns true if `x` is a number: int, float, `Ratio`, `BigInt`, or `BigDecimal`.

name: numerator
doc: Returns the numerator of `r`. For rationals the numerator collapses to a PHP int when it fits; for plain ints and `BigInt` values `r` is returned unchanged.

name: object-array
doc:
Creates a PHP array of the given size initialized to `nil`, or a PHP
  array containing the elements of the given sequence. Matches Clojure's
  `object-array` for `.cljc` interop — in Phel the result is a plain PHP
  array (accessible via `aget`/`aset`) since PHP has no typed
  array distinction.

name: odd?
doc: Checks if `x` is odd.

name: one?
doc: Checks if `x` is one.

name: or
doc: Evaluates expressions left to right, returning the first truthy value or the last value.

name: pairs
doc: Gets the pairs of an associative data structure.

name: parents
doc: Returns the set of immediate parents of tag, or nil. When a hierarchy is provided, consults it; otherwise uses the global hierarchy.

name: parse-boolean
doc:
Parses a string as a boolean. Returns `true` for the exact string
  `"true"`, `false` for `"false"`, and `nil` for any other input.
  The match is case-sensitive and does not tolerate surrounding
  whitespace.

name: parse-double
doc: Parses a string as a float. Returns `nil` for non-numeric input or for inputs that are not strings. Accepts `Infinity`, `-Infinity`, and `NaN` alongside regular decimal and scientific notation.

name: parse-long
doc: Parses a string as an integer. Returns nil if parsing fails.

name: parse-uuid
doc:
Parses `s` as a canonical UUID string and returns a `Phel\Lang\UUID`
  value, or nil if `s` is not a valid canonical UUID. Already-typed
  `UUID` values pass through unchanged.

name: partial
doc: Takes a function `f` and fewer than the normal number of arguments to `f`, and returns a function that takes a variable number of additional arguments. When called, `f` will be invoked with the bound `args` prepended to the additional arguments.

name: partition
doc:
Partitions `coll` into chunks of `n` elements.

  With one collection argument, returns consecutive non-overlapping chunks and drops any incomplete final chunk. `step` (default `n`) is how far to advance between chunks, so a `step` smaller than `n` yields overlapping chunks. With a `pad` collection, a final incomplete chunk is filled from `pad` up to `n` elements (kept even when `pad` runs short); without `pad` the incomplete final chunk is dropped. Each chunk is a vector.

name: partition-all
doc: Partitions collection into chunks of size `n`, including any incomplete trailing chunks. `step` (default `n`) is how far to advance between chunks, so a `step` smaller than `n` yields overlapping chunks. Each chunk is a vector.

name: partition-by
doc: Returns a lazy sequence of partitions. Applies `f` to each value in `coll`, splitting them each time the return value changes.

name: path-status-silenced
doc:
Answers `:directory`, `:file` or `:absent` for `path` with warnings off: a
  scheme-shaped path no wrapper answers to makes both checks warn, and the
  caller reports what went wrong itself.

name: peek
doc: Returns the head of a vector / PHP array (the last element) or the head of a list / lazy sequence / queue (the first element). Returns nil if `coll` is empty or nil.

name: persistent
doc: Converts a transient collection back to a persistent collection.

name: persistent!
doc: Converts a transient collection back to a persistent collection. Alias for `persistent`, matching Clojure's `persistent!` naming.

name: phel->php
doc: Recursively converts a Phel data structure to a PHP array.

name: phel->php-key
doc:
Converts a Phel map key into a valid PHP array key: named keys
  (keyword/symbol) use their name, scalar `int`/`string` keys pass through
  unchanged, and anything else is stringified.

name: php->phel
doc:
Recursively converts a PHP array to Phel data structures.

Indexed PHP arrays become vectors, associative PHP arrays become maps.

name: php-array-to-map
doc: Converts a PHP Array to a Phel map.

name: php-array?
doc: Returns true if `x` is a PHP Array, false otherwise.

name: php-associative-array
doc:
Creates a PHP associative array from key-value pairs.

  Arguments:
    Key-value pairs (must be even number of arguments)

name: php-class-relations
doc: Returns PHP parent classes and implemented interfaces for a class tag.

name: php-class-tag?
doc: Returns true when tag is a PHP class/interface/trait name string.

name: php-indexed-array
doc: Creates a PHP indexed array from the given values.

name: php-invoke
doc:
Calls the method `method` on `target`, where the method name is a value
  rather than a literal. `target` is either an object or a class-name string
  for a static method. Matches ClojureScript's `js-invoke`; use the dot
  syntax (`(.format d "Y")`) whenever the name is known at compile time.

name: php-object?
doc: Returns true if `x` is a PHP object, false otherwise.

name: php-resource?
doc: Returns true if `x` is a PHP resource, false otherwise.

name: pmap
doc:
Like `map`, but applies `f` to elements concurrently via fibers.

Returns a vector of results in the original order. With multiple collections, applies `f` to corresponding elements from each collection, stopping when the shortest collection is exhausted.

PHP fibers are cooperative on a single thread, so `pmap` overlaps IO-bound work (HTTP, DB, file IO) but does not parallelize CPU-bound computations across cores — unlike `clojure.core/pmap`, which uses a thread pool. ClojureScript and Basilisp follow the same single-threaded model.

name: pop
doc: Removes the last element of a collection. Returns nil for nil.

name: pop!
doc: Removes the last element from a transient vector, mutating it in place. Raises `InvalidArgumentException` when `tcoll` is not a transient vector. Matches Clojure's `pop!` semantics.

name: pop*
doc: Removes the last element of `coll`. Returns nil for nil or empty PHP arrays.

name: pos-int?
doc: Returns true if `x` is a positive integer (greater than zero). Accepts both fixed-precision PHP `int` and arbitrary-precision `BigInt` values.

name: pos?
doc: Checks if `x` is greater than zero.

name: pr
doc: Same as `print`, but prints each value readably (strings quoted). Returns nil.

name: pr-str
doc: Same as `print-str`, but prints each value readably: strings are quoted and escaped so the output can be read back. Phel has no dedicated char type, so character literals such as `\A` are single-character strings and print as `"A"` (ClojureScript-aligned; Clojure/JVM would print `\A`).

name: prefer-method
doc:
Causes the multimethod to prefer matches of `dispatch-val-x` over
  `dispatch-val-y` when there is an ambiguity (both match via the hierarchy
  and neither is more specific). Preferences are transitive.

  Throws if the new preference would create a cycle, i.e. `y` is already
  (transitively) preferred over `x`.

name: prefers
doc: Returns the preference map for a multimethod (built by `prefer-method`). Keys are dispatch values; values are sets of dispatch values they are preferred over (directly; preference is transitive when consulted).

name: prefers?
doc: Returns true if dispatch value `x` is preferred over `y` in `prefers-map`, considering transitive preferences. Used by multimethod dispatch when multiple methods match and the hierarchy does not pick a unique winner.

name: preserving-reduced
doc: Wraps a reducing function so Reduced propagates as double-wrapped.

name: print
doc: Prints the given values to the default output stream. Returns nil.

name: print-joined
doc: Space-joins `xs`, stringifying each element with `printer`.

name: print-str
doc: Same as print. But instead of writing it to an output stream, the resulting string is returned.

name: printf
doc: Output a formatted string. See PHP's [printf](https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.printf.php) for more information.

name: println
doc: Same as print followed by a newline.

name: println-str
doc: Same as `println`, but instead of writing to an output stream the resulting string is returned, with a trailing newline.

name: prn
doc: Same as `pr` followed by a newline. Returns nil.

name: prn-str
doc: Same as `prn`, but instead of writing to an output stream the resulting string is returned, with a trailing newline.

name: project
doc: Returns a set of maps, keeping only the keys in `ks` from each map in the relation `xrel`.

name: promise
doc:
Returns a new unrealized promise. Deliver a value with `(deliver p v)` and read it back with `@p` (or `(deref p)`).

Once delivered the value is frozen; subsequent `deliver` calls are no-ops. `deref` on an unrealized promise blocks: from inside a fiber it suspends cooperatively, from the top level it drains the scheduler ready queue and sleeps briefly between checks.

name: protocol-relations
doc: Returns the set of protocol values registered for a PHP class tag. Hierarchy-independent: surfaced by every `parents`/`ancestors`/`descendants` call, mirroring PHP class inheritance.

name: protocol-type-key
doc:
Returns the dispatch key for protocol dispatch. Returns a type keyword
  for primitive types, or the PHP class name string for objects/structs.

  Optimized to avoid the full `type` cond chain: checks scalars first
  (most common in tight loops), then objects.

name: push-binding-triple
doc: Appends a `[binding verb coll-expr]` triple to the normalized doseq head.

name: queue
doc: Creates a persistent FIFO queue. With no arguments returns an empty queue; with arguments returns a queue with the values pushed in order so that the first argument is at the front.

name: queue?
doc: Returns true if `x` is a `Phel\Lang\Collections\Queue\PersistentQueue` value.

name: quot
doc: Returns the truncated integer quotient of `dividend` / `divisor`. Truncates toward zero. Throws `DivisionByZeroError` when `divisor` is zero.

name: rand
doc: Without arguments, returns a random number in `[0, 1)`. With one argument `n`, returns a random number in `[0, n)`.

name: rand-int
doc: Returns a random number between 0 and `n`.

name: rand-nth
doc: Returns a random item from xs.

name: random-sample
doc: Returns the items of `coll` for which `(rand)` is less than `prob`, so each item is kept independently with probability `prob` (0 keeps nothing, 1 keeps everything). Lazy. Without a collection, returns a transducer.

name: random-uuid
doc: Returns a random version 4 UUID as a `Phel\Lang\UUID` value.

name: range
doc: Creates a lazy sequence of numbers. With no arguments returns an infinite sequence starting at 0. With one argument returns (0..n). With two (start..end). With three (start..end step). Note: the infinite sequence is bounded by PHP_INT_MAX.

name: ratio?
doc: Returns true if `x` is a `Ratio` value. Integer-valued rationals auto-collapse to `int`/`BigInt` at construction time, so `(ratio? 2/2)` is `false`.

name: rational?
doc: Returns true if `x` is a rational number: an integer (`int` or `BigInt`), a `Ratio`, or a `BigDecimal`. Floating-point numbers (including `##Inf`, `##-Inf`, and `##NaN`) are not rational.

name: rationalize
doc: Converts `x` to a `Ratio`. Floats use the shortest decimal expansion that round-trips back to the same float, so `(rationalize 0.1)` is `1/10` rather than the float-noise denominator. Ints, `BigInt`, and integer-valued `BigDecimal` values become `n/1` and auto-collapse, so they are returned as the integer value. `BigDecimal` with a fractional part rationalizes through its canonical decimal form.

name: re-find
doc: Returns the first match of pattern in string, or nil if no match. If the pattern has groups, returns a vector of [full-match group1 group2 ...].

name: re-matches
doc: Returns the match, if any, of string to pattern. If the pattern has groups, returns a vector of [full-match group1 group2 ...]. Returns nil if no match. Unlike re-find, the entire string must match.

name: re-pattern
doc: Returns a PCRE pattern string from `s`. If `s` is already delimited, returns it as-is. Otherwise wraps in `/` delimiters.

name: re-seq
doc: Returns a sequence of successive matches of pattern in string.

name: read-file-lazy
doc: Returns a lazy sequence of byte chunks from a file.

name: read-string
doc: Reads the first phel expression from the string s.

name: realized?
doc: Returns true if a lazy sequence, delay, promise, or future has been realized, false otherwise.

name: rebuild-hierarchy
doc: Rebuilds :ancestors and :descendants maps from the :parents map in h.

name: reduce
doc: Reduces collection to a single value by repeatedly applying function to accumulator and elements. Respects early termination via `(reduced val)`.

name: reduce-kv
doc: Reduces an associative collection by applying `f` to the accumulator, key and value of each entry, starting with `init`. Vectors use the index as key. Respects early termination via `(reduced val)`.

name: reduced
doc: Wraps `x` in a Reduced, signaling early termination from reduce/transduce.

name: reduced?
doc: Returns true if `x` is a Reduced value.

name: reductions
doc: Returns a lazy sequence of the intermediate values of the reduction (as per reduce) of coll by f, starting with init when supplied.

name: register-protocol-implementor!
doc:
Records that `type-key` implements the protocol identified by both
  `protocol-value` (the `defprotocol` map) and `protocol-tag` (its FQN
  string). Called from `extend-type`'s expansion.

name: reify
doc:
Creates an anonymous object implementing one or more protocols.
  Method bodies close over local bindings. Each instance carries its
  own captured state, so reify works correctly inside loops.

  Syntax:
    (reify
      ProtocolName
      (method-name [this arg1] body)
      AnotherProtocol
      (another-method [this] body))

name: rem
doc: Returns the truncated remainder of `dividend` / `divisor`. The result has the same sign as `dividend` (matches PHP's `%`).

name: remove
doc: Returns a lazy sequence of elements where predicate returns false. Opposite of filter. When called with pred only, returns a transducer.

name: remove-ns
doc: Removes the namespace and all of its definitions from the registry. Use with caution. Returns nil.

name: remove-tap
doc: Removes `f` from the tap set. Returns nil.

name: remove-watch
doc: Removes a watch function from a variable by key.

name: rename
doc: Returns a set of maps like the relation `xrel`, with the keys of each map renamed according to `kmap` (a map of old-key to new-key).

name: rename-keys
doc: Returns the map with keys renamed according to kmap. Keys not present in kmap are left unchanged.

name: repeat
doc:
Returns a vector of length n where every element is x.

With one argument returns an infinite lazy sequence of x.

name: repeatedly
doc:
Returns a vector of length n with values produced by repeatedly calling f.

With one argument returns an infinite lazy sequence of calls to f.

name: reset-meta!
doc: Installs `meta-map` as the metadata on `r`, replacing any prior metadata. Works on `Var` handles and on atoms. Returns the installed map.

name: reset-vals!
doc: Sets the value of the atom `variable` to `new-value`. Returns a vector `[old-value new-value]` of the values before and after the reset.

name: reset!
doc: Sets a new value on the given atom. Returns the new value.

name: resolve
doc: Resolves the given symbol in the current environment and returns a resolved Symbol with the absolute namespace or nil if it cannot be resolved.

name: rest
doc: Returns the sequence after the first element, or empty sequence if none.

name: reverse
doc: Reverses the order of the elements in the given sequence.

name: reversible?
doc: Returns true if `coll` can be reverse-iterated in constant time. Currently this is true for vectors, sorted-maps, and sorted-sets.

name: round
doc: Rounds `x` to the nearest integer using PHP's `round` (half away from zero). Ints and `BigInt` values are returned unchanged. Ratios and floats return floats.

name: rseq
doc: Returns, in constant time, a sequence of the items in `rev` in reverse order. `rev` must be reversible (a vector, sorted-map, or sorted-set); otherwise an exception is thrown. For sorted-maps, returns reversed `[key value]` pairs. Returns nil if `rev` is empty.

name: rsubseq
doc: Like `subseq`, but returns the matching entries in descending order. With one boundary, use `<` / `<=` to start from the top end and `>` / `>=` to stop; with two boundaries, returns the entries between them in reverse, e.g. `(rsubseq sm >= 2 < 5)`.

name: run!
doc: Calls `(f x)` for each element in `coll` for side effects. Returns nil.

name: satisfies?
doc: Returns true if x's type implements all methods of the given protocol.

name: second
doc: Returns the second element of a sequence, or nil if not present.

name: select
doc: Returns a set of the elements of `xset` for which `(pred element)` is logical true.

name: select-keys
doc: Returns a new map including key value pairs from `m` selected with keys `ks`.

name: seq
doc:
Returns a seq on the collection. Strings are converted to a vector of characters. Other non-empty collections (vectors, sets, sorted-maps, sorted-sets, PHP arrays) are converted to a non-list seq. Returns nil if `coll` is empty or nil.

This function is useful for explicitly converting strings to sequences of characters, enabling sequence operations like map, filter, and frequencies.

name: seq?
doc:
Returns true if `x` is a seq (a list, a lazy sequence, or a realized
  `Cons` cell returned by `(next some-lazy-seq)`).

name: seqable?
doc: Returns true if `(seq x)` is supported: collections (vectors, lists, maps, sets, structs), lazy sequences, strings, PHP arrays, and nil. Returns false for numbers, booleans, keywords, symbols, and other types.

name: sequence
doc: Applies transducer `xform` to `coll`, returning a vector of results.

name: sequential?
doc: Returns true if `x` is a sequential collection (vector, list, or lazy sequence), false otherwise. Sequential collections maintain insertion order and support indexed or linear access. Maps, sets, and structs are not sequential, matching Clojure's `Sequential` marker.

name: set
doc: Coerces a collection to a set. Returns a set containing the distinct elements of `coll`. For creating sets from arguments, use `hash-set`.

name: set-validator!
doc: Sets a validator function on a variable. The validator is called before any state change with the proposed new value. If it returns a falsy value, an exception is thrown and the state is not changed. Pass nil to remove.

name: set!
doc:
Sets `place` to `value` and returns `value`, covering all three shapes
  Clojure's `set!` covers.

  A property access (`(.-prop obj)`) assigns the property, as does any other
  place `php/oset` accepts. A **qualified symbol naming a member of a PHP
  class** (`Foo/slot`) assigns that static property. Any other **symbol**
  names a dynamic var and assigns its current thread-local binding, throwing
  when no `binding` frame is active, so it never writes the root by accident;
  `alter-var-root` is the way to change a root.

  A macro rather than a function because the place is a location, not a value.

name: set?
doc: Returns true if `x` is a set, false otherwise.

name: short
doc: Coerces `x` to a signed 16-bit integer in the range `-32768..32767`. Decimal values are truncated toward zero. `Ratio` and `BigInt` values are accepted (truncate toward zero, then range-check). Values outside the range or non-numeric inputs raise `InvalidArgumentException`. Phel has no dedicated short type, so the result is a plain PHP int.

name: short-array
doc: Creates a PHP array of shorts (16-bit integers). Accepts the same arities and semantics as `int-array`.

name: shuffle
doc: Returns a random permutation of coll.

name: simple-ident?
doc: Returns true if `x` is a symbol or keyword without a namespace.

name: simple-keyword?
doc: Returns true if `x` is a keyword without a namespace.

name: simple-symbol?
doc: Returns true if `x` is a symbol without a namespace.

name: slice
doc: Extracts a slice of `coll` starting at `offset` with optional `length`.

name: slurp
doc: Reads an entire file, URL or stream into a string.

name: some
doc: Returns the first truthy value of applying predicate to elements, or nil if none found.

name: some->
doc: Threads `x` through the forms like `->` but stops when a form returns `nil`.

name: some->>
doc: Threads `x` through the forms like `->>` but stops when a form returns `nil`.

name: some-fn
doc: Takes a variadic set of predicates and returns a function `f` that, when called with any number of arguments, returns the first logical true value produced by applying any of the composing predicates to any of its arguments, and `false` when none match. The returned function short-circuits on the first truthy result: arguments after it are not inspected, and predicates after it are not tried. Predicates are consulted in the order supplied; for a given predicate, arguments are consulted left-to-right.
example:
((some-fn even? nil?) 1 2) ; => true
((some-fn pos? even?) -3 -1) ; => false

name: some?
doc: With 1 arg, returns true if `x` is not nil (Clojure semantics). With 2 args, returns true if `pred` is true for at least one element in `coll`.

name: sort
doc: Returns a sorted vector. If no comparator is supplied compare is used.

name: sort-by
doc:
Returns a sorted vector where the sort order is determined by comparing `(keyfn item)`.

If no comparator is supplied compare is used.

name: sort-by-with
doc:
Decorate, sort, undecorate. Building the comparator as
  `#(cmp (keyfn %1) (keyfn %2))` runs `keyfn` twice per comparison, so O(n log n)
  times: sorting 100 elements called it 1114 times to derive 100 keys. Computing
  each key once up front and sorting `[key value]` pairs calls it exactly n
  times, and the gap widens with n (#3006).

  This is an observable divergence from Clojure, whose `sort-by` calls `keyfn`
  per comparison as this one used to. It is invisible to a pure key function,
  which is the normal case, and visible to one that counts calls, logs or
  memoises. Recorded in `docs/spec/clojure-divergences.md`.

  `php/aget` rather than `aget` inside the comparator: `aget` is a function, so
  it would add two Phel calls per comparison and give back a good part of what
  the transform buys.

name: sort-comparator
doc: Wraps the user-supplied comparator (or `compare` when absent) so its result is always an integer. A predicate-style comparator that returns a boolean follows Clojure semantics: a truthy result means the first argument should sort earlier (`-1`), the reverse-truthy case means it should sort later (`+1`), otherwise the items are considered equal.

name: sorted-bound-fn
doc:
Boundary predicate for subseq/rsubseq: true when the element's key (for a
  sorted map) or the element itself (for a sorted set) satisfies
  `(test (cmp k bound-key) 0)` under the collection's own comparator.

name: sorted-map
doc: Creates a new sorted map. Keys are in natural sorted order. The number of parameters must be even.

name: sorted-map-by
doc: Creates a new sorted map using the given comparator for key ordering. The comparator takes two arguments and returns a negative integer, zero, or a positive integer.
example: (sorted-map-by (fn [a b] (compare b a)) :a 1 :b 2) ; keys iterate as :b :a

name: sorted-set
doc: Creates a new sorted set. Elements are in natural sorted order.

name: sorted-set-by
doc: Creates a new sorted set using the given comparator for element ordering.

name: sorted-vector-natural
doc:
`sort` with no comparator, where `usort` would call back into Phel twice per
  comparison: once for the `sort-comparator` wrapper and once for `compare`,
  O(n log n) times. When every element is a native int, `SORT_NUMERIC` produces
  exactly the order `compare` produces, and PHP does the whole sort natively.
  One O(n) scan buys that, which is cheaper than the calls it replaces.

name: sorted?
doc: Returns true if `coll` is a sorted collection (sorted-map or sorted-set), false otherwise.

name: special-symbol?
doc: Returns true if `s` names a special form.

name: special-symbols
doc:
The set of symbols that name Phel special forms, including the
  syntactic markers `&`, `catch`, and `finally` recognised by `fn`,
  `let`, and `try`.

name: spit
doc:
Writes data to file, returning number of bytes that were written or `nil` on failure. Accepts `opts` map for overriding default PHP file_put_contents arguments, as example to append to file use `{:flags php/FILE_APPEND}`.

See PHP's [file_put_contents](https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.file-put-contents.php) for more information.

name: split-at
doc: Returns a vector of `[(take n coll) (drop n coll)]`.

name: split-with
doc: Returns a vector of `[(take-while pred coll) (drop-while pred coll)]`.

name: splitv-at
doc: Returns a vector `[(vec (take n coll)) (vec (drop n coll))]`. Like `split-at`, but eagerly returns vectors rather than lazy sequences.

name: sqrt
doc:
Returns the square root of `x` as a float. Negative inputs return
  `##NaN` (matches PHP's `sqrt`).

name: static-property-place?
doc:
True when `place` is a symbol naming a static property. Both halves restate
  the analyzer's `QualifiedMemberSyntax`, which the standard library cannot
  import: the namespace reads as a PHP class reference (a leading `\` or an
  upper-case first character) and the name starts like a PHP member, optionally
  carrying the `$` sigil. A dynamic var fails the second half, since `Foo/*x*`
  is no member PHP can name, and stays a var.

name: str
doc: Creates a string by concatenating values together. If no arguments are provided an empty string is returned. Nil is represented as an empty string. Booleans are represented as "true" or "false" (matching Clojure semantics). Otherwise, it tries to call `__toString`.

name: stream-path?
doc:
True when `path` reads through a registered stream wrapper (`https://`,
  `data://`, `php://stdin`, `phar://`, whatever the host registered) rather
  than naming a file on disk. A scheme no wrapper answers to counts as a path,
  because that is what PHP does with it, and because a relative directory may
  legally be named `something:` and be followed by a slash.

name: string?
doc: Returns true if `x` is a string, false otherwise.

name: struct?
doc: Returns true if `x` is a struct, false otherwise.

name: subseq
doc: Returns a lazy sequence of the entries of the sorted collection `sc` (map entries for a sorted map, elements for a sorted set) whose keys satisfy the boundary test, in ascending order. With one boundary, use `>` / `>=` to start after or at `bound-key` and `<` / `<=` to stop before or at it. With two boundaries, returns the entries between them, e.g. `(subseq sm >= 2 < 5)`. Boundaries respect the collection's own comparator (`sorted-map-by` / `sorted-set-by`).

name: subset?
doc: Returns true if `s1` is a subset of `s2`, i.e. every element in `s1` is also in `s2`.

name: subvec
doc: Returns a persistent vector of the items in `v` from `start` (inclusive) to `end` (exclusive). `end` defaults to `(count v)`. Non-integer indices truncate toward zero and `NaN` counts as `0`, matching Clojure. The result shares structure with `v`. Throws an OutOfBoundsException when `start` or `end` is out of range or `start` is greater than `end`.

name: sum
doc: Returns the sum of all elements is `xs`.

name: superset?
doc: Returns true if `s1` is a superset of `s2`, i.e. every element in `s2` is also in `s1`.

name: swap-vals!
doc: Atomically swaps the value of the atom `variable` to `(apply f current-value args)`. Returns a vector `[old-value new-value]` of the values before and after the swap.

name: swap!
doc:
Atomically swaps the value of the atom to `(apply f current-value args)`.

Returns the new value after the swap.

name: symbol
doc:
Returns a new symbol for the given name with an optional namespace.

With one argument, creates a symbol without namespace. Accepts a string, a keyword, another symbol, or a `Var` (in which case the result is a fully qualified symbol naming the var). With two arguments, creates a symbol in the given namespace; a `nil` namespace yields a symbol without a namespace.

Throws `InvalidArgumentException` for any other input (including functions, numbers, and collections).

name: symbol?
doc: Returns true if `x` is a symbol, false otherwise.

name: symmetric-difference
doc: Symmetric difference between multiple sets into a new one.

name: take
doc: Takes the first `n` elements of `coll`. When called with n only, returns a transducer.

name: take-last
doc: Takes the last `n` elements of `coll`.

name: take-nth
doc: Returns every nth item in `coll`. Returns a lazy sequence. When called with n only, returns a transducer.

name: take-while
doc: Takes all elements at the front of `coll` where `(pred x)` is true. Returns a lazy sequence. When called with pred only, returns a transducer.

name: tap>
doc: Sends `x` to every registered tap. Exceptions thrown by individual taps are swallowed so one misbehaving tap does not affect the others. Returns true.

name: thread-bound?
doc: Returns true when a fiber-local `binding` (or `with-bindings`) frame currently overrides the value of `v` on the calling fiber.

name: time
doc: Evaluates expr and prints the time it took. Returns the value of expr.

name: to-array
doc: Returns a PHP array containing the elements of `coll`. Accepts any collection (vector, list, set, map, PHP array) or `nil`, which yields an empty PHP array. Matches Clojure's `to-array` for `.cljc` interop — in Phel the result is a plain PHP array since PHP has no `Object[]`.

name: to-php-array
doc: Creates a PHP Array from a sequential data structure.

name: to-symbol-part
doc: Extracts the underlying string from `x` for use as a symbol or namespace component. Keywords and symbols pass through their `name`.

name: trampoline
doc: Calls `f` with any supplied `args`. While the return value is a function, calls it with no arguments and repeats; returns the first non-function value. Use it for stack-safe mutual recursion: have the functions return a zero-argument function wrapping the next call instead of calling it directly. Only Phel functions bounce — keywords and collections, although callable, are returned as-is. To return a function as the final value, wrap it in a collection and unwrap it after `trampoline` returns.

name: transduce
doc:
Reduce with a transformation of `f` (xf). If init is not supplied,
  `(f)` will be called to produce it. `f` should be a reducing function
  that returns the initial value when called with no arguments.

name: transient
doc:
Converts a persistent collection to a transient collection for efficient updates.

Transient collections provide faster performance for multiple sequential updates. Use `persistent` to convert back.

name: tree-seq
doc: Returns a vector of the nodes in the tree, via a depth-first walk. branch? is a function with one argument that returns true if the given node has children. children must be a function with one argument that returns the children of the node. root the root node of the tree.

name: true?
doc: Checks if value is exactly true (not just truthy).

name: truthy?
doc: Checks if `x` is truthy. Same as `x == true` in PHP.

name: type
doc:
Returns the type of `x`. The following types can be returned:

* `:vector`
* `:list`
* `:struct`
* `:hash-map`
* `:map-entry`
* `:set`
* `:keyword`
* `:symbol`
* `:atom`
* `:var`
* `:int`
* `:float`
* `:ratio`
* `:bigint`
* `:bigdec`
* `:uuid`
* `:php/class`
* `:queue`
* `:string`
* `:nil`
* `:boolean`
* `:function`
* `:php/array`
* `:php/resource`
* `:php/object`
* `:unknown`

name: underive
doc: Removes a parent/child relationship. With two arguments, mutates the global hierarchy and returns nil. With a hierarchy `h`, returns a new hierarchy without the relationship; the original is unchanged.

name: union
doc: Union multiple sets into a new one.

name: union-target
doc:
A transient set seeded from `coll`. When `coll` is already a set the
  transient starts from it directly; `union` also accepts any other iterable,
  and those still have to be added element by element.

name: unreduced
doc: If `x` is Reduced, returns the unwrapped value; otherwise returns `x`.

name: unsigned-bit-shift-right
doc: Bitwise shift right without sign extension: the vacated high bits are filled with zeros rather than copies of the sign bit. Unlike `bit-shift-right`, `(unsigned-bit-shift-right -1 10)` is a large positive number, not `-1`.

name: unwrap-future
doc: Returns the raw Amp\Future for either a `Future` wrapper or a bare `Amp\Future`.

name: update
doc: Updates a value in a datastructure by applying `f` to the current value.

name: update-in
doc: Updates a value in a nested data structure by applying `f` to the value at path.

name: update-keys
doc: Returns a map with `f` applied to each key.

name: update-vals
doc: Returns a map with `f` applied to each value.

name: uuid-nil?
doc: Returns true if `x` is the nil UUID (all zeros), false otherwise.

name: uuid-variant
doc:
Returns a keyword describing the variant field of UUID `x`: `:ncs`,
  `:rfc-4122`, `:microsoft`, or `:reserved`. Returns nil if `x` is not a
  `UUID` value.

name: uuid-version
doc: Returns the version digit (1-5) encoded in UUID `x`, or nil if `x` is not a `UUID` value.

name: uuid?
doc: Returns true if `x` is a `Phel\Lang\UUID` value, false otherwise. Canonical UUID strings are rejected — wrap them with `parse-uuid` (or the `#uuid "..."` literal) to obtain a typed value.

name: uuid=
doc: Returns true if `a` and `b` are `Phel\Lang\UUID` values with the same canonical form. Strings (or anything else) are rejected even if their textual content would match — coerce with `parse-uuid` first.

name: val
doc:
Returns the value of a map entry. Accepts a typed
  `Phel\Lang\Collections\Map\MapEntry` value or a 2-element vector
  `[key value]`.

name: val-to-str
doc: Converts a value to its string representation. Booleans become "true" or "false". Nil becomes an empty string. Integer-valued floats keep their `.0` suffix (so `(str 0.0)` is `"0.0"`, not `"0"`). All other values use PHP string cast.

name: valid-global-child-tag?
doc: Returns true when tag is valid as a child in the global hierarchy.

name: valid-global-parent-tag?
doc: Returns true when tag is valid as a parent in the global hierarchy.

name: valid-hierarchy-parents
doc: Returns h's parents map when h has the expected hierarchy shape.

name: vals
doc: Returns a sequence of all values in a map, or `nil` when the map is `nil` or empty.

name: var-get
doc:
Resolves the value bound to a `Var` or to a fully-qualified symbol.

  Accepts a `Var` instance (typically from `(var sym)` or `#'sym`) and
  returns its current root value. Accepts a fully-qualified symbol and
  reads the matching definition from the registry; tries the symbol name
  verbatim first, then the encoded form, so it pairs with both `def` and
  `intern`.

  With one argument, returns nil when the symbol is not defined. With two
  arguments, returns `not-found` instead, which lets callers disambiguate a
  stored nil from a missing definition. Returns `not-found` for non-symbol
  or unqualified inputs.

name: var-set
doc:
Sets the value of the topmost active fiber-local binding frame for
  `v` to `val`. Throws when no `binding` (or `with-bindings`) frame is
  currently overriding `v`. Returns `val`.

name: var?
doc: Returns true if the given value is a `Var`, the first-class handle to a global definition produced by `(var sym)` and `#'sym`.

name: variadic?
doc: Returns true if the function `f` accepts a variable number of arguments. A multi-arity function compiles to a single variadic dispatch, so it always reports `true`.

name: vary-meta
doc: Returns an object with (apply f (meta obj) args) as its new metadata.

name: vec
doc: Coerces a collection to a vector. For hash-maps and structs, entries are returned as 2-element `[key value]` vectors, matching Clojure.

name: vector
doc: Creates a new vector. If no argument is provided, an empty vector is created. Shortcut: []

name: vector-assoc
doc: Updates a vector at an integer index. Vectors index by int only; a non-integer key raises a clean `InvalidArgumentException` instead of leaking PHP's `update(): Argument #1 ($i) must be of type int` TypeError.

name: vector?
doc: Returns true if `x` is a vector. Map entries returned by iterating a hash map (`(first {:a 1})`) are vector-shaped two-element values, so this predicate also accepts the typed `MapEntry`.

name: volatile!
doc: Creates a volatile mutable reference with initial value `val`. Use for transducer state that needs fast mutation without watches.

name: volatile?
doc: Returns true if `x` is a Volatile.

name: vreset!
doc: Sets the value of volatile `vol` to `val`. Returns `val`.

name: vswap!
doc: Applies `f` to the current value of volatile `vol` plus `args`, and sets the new value. Returns the new value.

name: when
doc: Evaluates body if test is true, otherwise returns nil.

name: when-first
doc:
Binds name to the first element of coll. When the collection is non-empty
  (first returns non-nil), evaluates body with the binding.

name: when-let
doc: When test is true, evaluates body with binding-form bound to the value of test

name: when-not
doc: Evaluates body if test is false, otherwise returns nil.

name: when-some
doc: Binds name to the value of test. When test is not nil, evaluates body with binding-form bound to the value of test. Unlike when-let, false and 0 are not treated as falsy — only nil causes the body to be skipped.

name: while
doc: Repeatedly evaluates `body` (for side effects) as long as `test` is logical true. Returns nil.

name: with-bindings
doc: Like `binding` but takes a map of `Var -> value` instead of a binding vector. Same dynamic-only enforcement: throws when any key resolves to a non-dynamic var.

name: with-meta
doc: Returns `obj` with the given metadata `meta` attached.

name: with-open
doc:
Evaluates body with the names bound as in `let`, then closes every bound
  resource in a `finally` clause — in reverse binding order — even when the
  body throws. Objects exposing a `close` method are closed by calling it,
  stream resources with `php/fclose`; `nil` bindings are skipped.

name: with-output-buffer
doc: Everything that is printed inside the body will be stored in a buffer. The result of the buffer is returned.

name: with-redefs
doc:
Temporarily replaces the root values of vars while executing `body`.

  Accepts any var, dynamic or not. The previous root values are
  captured before `body` runs and restored on exit, including when
  `body` throws. The replacement is process-global: every fiber sees
  the new root for the duration of the body, which makes this a
  convenient mocking primitive for tests but unsafe for concurrent
  production code. Use `binding` for fiber-local rebinding of
  `^:dynamic` vars.

name: xf-step
doc: Creates a transducer reducing function that delegates 0/1 arity to rf and calls step-fn for the 2-arity step. Eliminates repeated boilerplate.

name: zero?
doc: Checks if `x` is zero.

name: zipcoll
doc: Creates a map from two sequential data structures. Returns a new map.

name: zipmap
doc:
Returns a new map with the keys mapped to the corresponding values.

Stops when the shorter of `keys` or `vals` is exhausted. Works safely with infinite lazy sequences.

name: install-readers
doc: Registers each `tag -> fn` from `readers` on the registry.

name: read-next
doc: Reads the next form from the open `token-stream` using `cf`. Skips whitespace, comments, and other trivia parser nodes that precede the next data form. Returns nil when the stream is exhausted.

name: read-string
doc:
Reads one EDN value from string `s`.

  When `s` is empty or only whitespace/comments, returns the `:eof` value
  from `opts` (default nil).

  Options:
    :readers  map of tag (symbol, keyword, or string) to 1-arg handler fn
    :eof      value returned for empty input

name: read-string-all
doc:
Reads every EDN value from string `s` and returns them as a vector.

  Options:
    :readers  map of tag (symbol, keyword, or string) to 1-arg handler fn

name: restore-tags
doc: Reinstates the original handlers captured by `snapshot-tags`. When a tag had no prior handler, it is unregistered so the registry returns to its earlier shape.

name: snapshot-tags
doc: Captures the existing handler for each tag key so it can be restored after the call. Returns a map `{tag-key handler-or-nil}`.

name: tag-key
doc: Normalises a tag from a symbol, keyword, or string to the string key used by the global `TagRegistry`.

name: with-readers*
doc: Runs `thunk` with `readers` temporarily installed on the tag registry. Restores prior state in a `finally` so exceptions still clean up.

name: write-string
doc: Serialises `value` to its EDN string representation. Uses Phel's readable printer so the output round-trips through `read-string` for all EDN-compatible values (nil, booleans, numbers, strings, keywords, symbols, lists, vectors, maps, sets, and built-in tagged literals such as `#uuid`).

name: write-string-all
doc: Serialises a sequence of values to EDN, separating top-level forms with a single space. Inverse of `read-string-all`.

name: compile-element
doc: Compiles a element.

name: doctype
doc:
Returns an HTML doctype declaration for the given type. Supports `:html4`,
  `:xhtml-strict`, `:xhtml-transitional`, and `:html5`. Defaults to `:html5`.

name: element-tag
doc: Validates the head of an element vector and returns it as a string.

name: escape-html
doc: Escapes HTML special characters to prevent XSS.

name: html
doc:
Compiles nested Phel vectors to HTML strings at compile-time. A vector
  `[tag attrs? children*]` becomes an element; `tag` is a keyword or string,
  the optional `attrs` is a map, and children are strings, keywords, raw
  strings, or nested vectors. Special list forms `for`, `if`, `when`, and
  `when-not` are supported for dynamic content.

name: render-children
doc:
Renders each child and joins them. Same reason as `render-attrs`: `map`
  returns a lazy sequence whose first chunk is realized on construction, and
  `apply str` then spreads it through the variadic arm of `str`.

name: render-element
doc:
Renders an Element.

  Deliberately does not go through `normalize-element`. That returns a tuple
  and, for the children, a fresh collection built with `apply list`. Both are
  allocated once per element and discarded immediately. Reading the tag
  and attributes by index and walking the children in place took a single
  `[:span {:class "x"} "0"]` from 17.7μs to 9.7μs.

name: unevaluated?
doc: An expression is unevaluated if it is a symbol or it is not quoted.

name: append-query-params
doc: Appends query parameters to a URL string.

name: build-headers-array
doc: Converts a Phel header map to a PHP associative array.

name: build-options-array
doc: Converts Phel options to a PHP associative array for the transport.

name: delete
doc: Makes a DELETE request. See `request` for available options.

name: get
doc: Makes a GET request. See `request` for available options.

name: head
doc: Makes a HEAD request. See `request` for available options.

name: key->string
doc: Converts a keyword or string key to its string form.

name: patch
doc: Makes a PATCH request. See `request` for available options.

name: post
doc: Makes a POST request. See `request` for available options.

name: put
doc: Makes a PUT request. See `request` for available options.

name: request
doc:
Makes an HTTP request and returns an http/response struct.

  `method` is a keyword or string (:get, :post, "PUT", etc.).
  `url` is the target URL string.
  `opts` is an optional map with:
    :headers          - Map of header name to value
    :body             - String request body
    :json             - Value to JSON-encode as body (sets Content-Type)
    :query-params     - Map of query parameters to append to URL
    :timeout          - Timeout in seconds as float (default 30.0)
    :follow-redirects - Follow HTTP redirects (default true)
    :verify-ssl       - Verify SSL certificates (default true)
signature: (request method url & [{:headers headers :body body :json json-body :query-params query-params :timeout timeout :follow-redirects follow-redirects :verify-ssl verify-ssl}])

name: transport-result->response
doc: Converts a transport result PHP array to an http/response struct.

name: content-type-base
doc:
Lowercased media type from the `:content-type` header with any parameters
  stripped (`application/json; charset=utf-8` => `application/json`).

name: decode-json-body
doc: Decodes a JSON request body. Returns nil for an empty or malformed body so handlers can distinguish 'no usable body' from a real value.

name: emit-response
doc: Emits the response by sending headers and outputting the body.

name: encode-utf-8-url
doc: Prepares utf-8 urls from php/parse-url.

name: files-from-globals
doc: Extracts uploaded files from `$_FILES` and normalizes them to uploaded-file structs. Handles both flat and nested file specs from multipart uploads. Returns a map of field name to uploaded-file(s).

name: get-method-from-globals
doc: Extracts the request method from `$_SERVER`.

name: headers-from-server
doc: Extracts all HTTP headers from the `$_SERVER` variable. Strips the `HTTP_` prefix, normalizes underscores to hyphens, handles `CONTENT_*` keys, and resolves `REDIRECT_*` keys. Returns a map with keyword keys.

name: host-and-port-from-globals
doc: Extract the host and port from the `$_SERVER` array.

name: html-response
doc:
Creates a response with `status` and an HTML `body` and a
  `Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8` header.

name: json-request-body
doc: Reads the raw request body from `php://input`, but only when the request declares a JSON content type. Other requests never touch the input stream.

name: json-response
doc:
Creates a response with `status` and a JSON-encoded `data` body and a
  `Content-Type: application/json` header.

name: request
signature: (request method ; HTTP Method ("GET", "POST", ...) uri ; URI headers ; Map with all headers parsed-body ; parsed body ($_POST form data, or decoded JSON body) query-params ; Map with all query parameters ($_GET) cookie-params ; Map with all cookie parameters ($_COOKIE) server-params ; Map with all server parameters ($_SERVER) uploaded-files ; Array of normalized uploaded files ($_FILES) version ; HTTP Version attributes ; consumer-specific data to enrich the request)

name: request-from-globals
doc: Extracts a request from `$_SERVER`, `$_GET`, `$_POST`, `$_COOKIE`, `$_FILES` and, for JSON requests, the raw request body (`php://input`). Requires a web request context (PHP-FPM, mod_php, or `php -S`); it cannot be used from the REPL or a CLI script - use `request-from-map` for testing.

name: request-from-globals-args
doc:
Extracts a request from args. The optional `raw-body` (the raw request body
  string) is decoded into `:parsed-body` when the `Content-Type` is
  `application/json`; form bodies still come from `post-parameter`.
example: (request-from-globals-args php/$_SERVER php/$_GET php/$_POST php/$_COOKIE php/$_FILES (php/file_get_contents "php://input")) ; => (phel.http.request "GET" (phel.http.uri ...) {...} nil {...} {...} {...} {...} "1.1" {})

name: request-from-map
doc:
Creates a request struct from a map. Supports the optional keys `:method`,
  `:uri` (a string parsed via `uri-from-string`, or a uri struct used as-is),
  `:headers`, `:parsed-body`, `:query-params`, `:cookie-params`,
  `:server-params`, `:uploaded-files`, `:version`, and `:attributes`. Missing
  keys default to nil, `{}`, `[]`, or `"1.1"` as appropriate.
signature: (request-from-map {:method method :uri uri :headers headers :parsed-body parsed-body :query-params query-params :cookie-params cookie-params :server-params server-params :uploaded-files uploaded-files :version version :attributes attributes})

name: resolve-parsed-body
doc: Resolves `:parsed-body`: form data from `$_POST`, a decoded JSON body, or nil. The `:content-type` header is parsed once and matched against both cases.

name: response-from-map
doc:
Creates a response struct from a map. Optional keys: `:status` (defaults
  200), `:headers` (`{}`), `:body` (`""`), `:version` (`"1.1"`), and
  `:reason` (auto-filled from the HTTP status code when omitted).

name: response-from-string
doc:
Creates a 200 OK response with the given body string. Shorthand for
  `(response-from-map {:body s})`.

name: uri
signature: (uri scheme userinfo host port path query fragment)

name: uri-from-globals
doc:
Extracts the URI from the `$_SERVER` variable. The scheme is read from
  `HTTP_X_FORWARDED_PROTO`, `REQUEST_SCHEME`, or `HTTPS`; the path from
  `REQUEST_URI`; and the host/port via the `$_SERVER` host fields. Returns a
  uri struct.

name: uri-from-string
doc: Parses a URI string into a uri struct. Handles UTF-8 URLs and IPv6 addresses in brackets. Throws `InvalidArgumentException` on a malformed string.

name: decode
doc: Decodes a JSON string to a Phel value.

name: decode-value
doc: Converts a JSON value to Phel format.

name: encode
doc: Encodes a Phel value to a JSON string.

name: encode-key
doc:
Encodes a map key. JSON object keys are always strings, and a PHP array
  float key would be truncated to an int, so floats are stringified here
  (values keep their numeric type via `encode-value`).

name: encode-value
doc: Converts a Phel value to JSON-compatible format.

name: valid-key?
doc: Checks if a value can be used as a JSON key.

name: and-checks
doc:
Combines a seq of boolean checks into a single expression, skipping
  `true` and collapsing a single check.

name: as-pattern?
doc: A `(pattern :as sym)` list: matches `pattern` and binds it to `sym`.

name: binding-symbol?
doc: A bare symbol that is neither the wildcard nor the rest marker.

name: compile-as
doc: (inner :as name): bind target to name, recurse on inner.

name: compile-clause
doc: Compiles one clause row into `[check bindings]`.

name: compile-guard
doc: (inner :guard pred): compile inner, and-combine with (pred target) evaluated in the context of the inner bindings so the guard can see bound symbols.

name: compile-map
doc: Map pattern: shape check, key-presence check, recurse on each value.

name: compile-or
doc: (:or p1 p2 ...): succeeds if any alternative matches. Alternatives may not introduce bindings (keeps v1 simple and predictable).

name: compile-pattern
doc: Dispatches on pattern shape and delegates to the kind-specific compiler. Returns `{:check expr :bindings [sym val ...]}`.

name: compile-vector
doc: Vector pattern: shape + length check, recursively compile each element, optionally bind the rest of the slice.

name: guard-pattern?
doc: A `(pattern :guard pred)` list: matches `pattern` then tests `pred`.

name: index-of-rest
doc: Linear scan for `&` inside a vector, comparing with `=` so that freshly-read symbols match the `'&` literal. Returns the index or nil.

name: match
doc:
Matches a vector of targets against pattern/expression clauses and
  returns the first matching expression.

  Supported patterns:
  - literal values (numbers, strings, keywords, booleans, nil)
  - `_` wildcard
  - bare symbol: binds the value to that name in the clause body
  - vector pattern `[a b c]`, with optional rest `[a & tail]`
  - map pattern `{:k1 p1 :k2 p2}` — keys must be present in the target
  - `(inner :guard pred)` — matches if `(pred bound)` is truthy
  - `(inner :as name)` — binds the whole value to `name`
  - `(:or p1 p2 ...)` — matches any alternative (no inner bindings)

  A trailing `:else expr` provides the default branch; without it a
  no-match raises `RuntimeException`.

name: or-pattern?
doc: An `(:or alt ...)` list: matches when any alternative matches.

name: parse-clauses
doc: Walks the body splitting it into `[clauses default]`. `clauses` is a vector of `[pattern-vec expr]`, `default` is the `:else` expression or `nil`.

name: scalar-literal?
doc: Primitives we should match by equality.

name: sequential-shape-check
doc: Runtime predicate accepting vectors, lists, and PHP arrays.

name: shape-gated-check
doc: Wraps an inner and-combined check behind a shape predicate. When the target fails the shape check the expression short-circuits to `false` so the inner accessors never see a mismatched value.

name: split-vector-pattern
doc: Splits a vector pattern around `&`. Returns `[head tail-sym-or-nil]`. Errors if `&` is not followed by exactly one symbol.

name: call-count
doc: Returns the number of times the mock was called.

name: called-once?
doc: Returns true if the mock was called exactly once.

name: called-times?
doc: Returns true if the mock was called exactly n times.

name: called-with?
doc: Returns true if the mock was called with the exact arguments.

name: called?
doc: Returns true if the mock was called at least once.

name: calls
doc: Returns a list of all argument lists the mock was called with.

name: clear-all-mocks!
doc: Clears the entire mock registry. Useful for cleanup between test suites in long-running processes.

name: first-call
doc: Returns the arguments from the first call.

name: get-mock-calls
doc: Gets the call history for a mock function

name: last-call
doc: Returns the arguments from the most recent call.

name: mock
doc: Creates a mock function that returns a fixed value and tracks all calls.

name: mock-fn
doc: Creates a mock function with custom behavior that tracks all calls.

name: mock-returning
doc: Creates a mock that returns different values for consecutive calls. After exhausting values, returns the last value.

name: mock-throwing
doc: Creates a mock that throws an exception when called.

name: mock?
doc: Returns true if the function is a mock.

name: never-called?
doc: Returns true if the mock was never called.

name: register-mock!
doc: Registers a mock function with its call history and optional reset function

name: reset-mock!
doc: Resets the call history of a mock without removing it from the registry. The mock can continue to be used and track new calls.

name: spy
doc: Wraps an existing function to track calls while preserving original behavior. Alias for `mock-fn`.

name: with-mock-wrapper
doc:
Like with-mocks but for wrapped mocks (interop scenarios).
  Automatically resets the underlying mock even when wrapped in an adapter function.

  Usage:
    ```phel
    (with-mock-wrapper [fn-symbol underlying-mock wrapper-fn]
      body...)
    ```

  Multiple wrappers:
    ```phel
    (with-mock-wrapper [service-a mock-a (fn [x] (mock-a (inc x)))
                        service-b mock-b (fn [y] (mock-b (dec y)))]
      ...)
    ```

name: with-mocks
doc:
Temporarily replaces functions with mocks using `with-redefs`.
  Automatically resets mocks after the body executes.

  Works with inline mock creation:
    ```phel
    (with-mocks [http-get (mock {:status 200})]
      (http-get)
      ;; Mock is automatically reset after this block)
    ```

  Also works with pre-defined mocks:
    ```phel
    (let [my-mock (mock :result)]
      (with-mocks [some-fn my-mock]
        (some-fn)))
    ```

  If you need to wrap the mock in a function (e.g., to adapt arguments),
  you'll need to manually reset:
    ```phel
    (with-mocks [some-fn (fn [& args] (my-mock (transform args)))]
      (some-fn)
      (reset-mock! my-mock))
    ```

name: color-output?
doc:
True when stdout is an interactive terminal.
  Output buffering means the text is being captured, not shown on a terminal.

name: inspect
doc: Pretty-prints `x` to stdout (colored on a TTY) and returns `x` unchanged.

name: pp-pairs
doc:
The same for a map or struct, where each entry is a key, a space, and its
  value laid out from just past the key.

name: pp-parts
doc:
Pretty-prints each element of `form` at `inner-indent`, joined by a newline
  and that much padding.

name: pp-str
doc:
Pretty-prints `form` to a string with the given indent level and max width.
  Width is always measured on the plain readable output; `printer` only affects
  how leaves are rendered (ANSI codes would inflate the measured length).

name: pprint
doc: Pretty-prints `form` to stdout with optional `width` (default 72).

name: pprint-str
doc: Pretty-prints `form` to a string with optional `width` (default 72).

name: print-value
doc:
Prints a scalar or non-collection value using the standard readable printer.
  The printer is built once: `Printer/readable` allocates, and this is called
  for every node the walk measures. `phel.edn` hoists the same way.

name: render-value
doc: Prints `x` with the given printer (plain or colored).

name: register-tag
doc:
Registers a handler for reader tag `tag-name` (a string without the leading `#`). The handler `f` is a 1-arg function receiving the already-read form value and returning the value that should replace the tagged literal.

Re-registering an existing tag overwrites the previous handler.

name: registered-tags
doc: Returns a sorted vector of the currently registered reader tag names.

name: registry
doc: Returns the shared TagRegistry singleton.

name: tag-registered?
doc: Returns true if a handler is registered for reader tag `tag-name`.

name: unregister-tag
doc: Removes any handler registered for reader tag `tag-name`. Built-in tags can be unregistered but are re-installed on the next reader bootstrap.

name: attribute-args
doc: Builds the `:args` map for a `ReflectionAttribute`: named arguments become keyword keys, positional arguments keep their integer index.

name: attributes
doc: Returns the class-level attribute maps for `obj-or-class`; an instance uses its class. Convenience alias of `class-attributes`.

name: class-attributes
doc: Returns a vector of attribute maps for the class `class-or-name` (string FQN or object). Each map is `{:name <attribute-fqcn> :args {...}}`, where `:args` keys named arguments as keywords and positional arguments by index.

name: class-info
doc:
Returns a map describing `class-or-name` with `:name`, `:methods`,
  `:properties`, `:parents`, and `:interfaces` keys.

name: enum->keyword
doc:
Returns the keyword for a native PHP enum `enum-case`, using the case name
  verbatim (`Status/Active` => `:Active`). Round-trips with `keyword->enum`.

name: enum-values
doc:
Returns a vector of keywords, one per case of the native PHP enum
  `enum-class` (string FQN), in declaration order.

name: keyword->enum
doc: Returns the case of the native PHP enum `enum-class` (string FQN) whose name matches keyword `kw`, or nil when no case matches. Inverse of `enum->keyword`.

name: method-attributes
doc: Returns a vector of attribute maps for method `method-name` on `class-or-name`.

name: methods
doc:
Returns a vector of method maps for `class-or-name`. Each map contains
  `:name`, `:params`, `:return-type`, `:static?`, and `:visibility`.

name: properties
doc:
Returns a vector of property maps for `class-or-name`. Each map contains
  `:name`, `:type`, `:static?`, `:readonly?`, and `:visibility`.

name: property-attributes
doc: Returns a vector of attribute maps for property `property-name` on `class-or-name`.

name: reflection-class
doc: Returns a ReflectionClass for `class-or-name` (string FQN or object).

name: supers
doc: Returns a set of fully qualified parent classes and implemented interfaces for `class-or-name`.

name: type-string
doc: Renders a ReflectionType (named, union, or intersection) as a string. Returns nil when the reflection type itself is nil (no declaration).

name: apropos
doc: Returns a vector of symbols whose name contains the given search string. Searches across all loaded namespaces.

name: build-namespace-context
doc: Builds a summary of available functions in the current namespace and its aliases for AI context.

name: build-symbol-context
doc: Builds AI context for a specific symbol: source code, docs, and metadata.

name: compile-str
doc:
Compiles a Phel expression string to PHP code and returns it, without evaluating it.

Compilation happens in expression context, so a bare top-level expression yields the PHP it reduces to rather than the empty string a statement-context compile would produce for a value nobody binds. Constant folding still applies, so `(+ 1 2)` compiles to `3`. Use `eval-str` to run the code instead of reading it.

name: create-ns
doc: Creates the given namespace if it does not already exist. Returns the namespace name in display form. Existing namespaces are left untouched.

name: dir
doc:
Prints all public definitions in the given namespace symbol or string.

Returns nil. Prints one name per line, sorted alphabetically.

name: dir-fn
doc:
Prints all public definitions in the given namespace symbol or string.

Returns nil. Prints one name per line, sorted alphabetically.

name: doc
doc: Prints the documentation for the given symbol.

name: embed-ns
doc:
Builds a searchable index of all public functions in a namespace.

Each entry contains the function name, docstring, and embedding of the combined name+doc text. Useful for semantic code search.

Options are passed through to `ai/embed`.

name: eval-capturing
doc:
Evaluates a string of Phel code while capturing stdout. Returns a hash-map
  with :value (the result), :out (captured stdout), :success (boolean), and
  :error (error message or nil).

  Useful for nREPL and other tooling that needs to separate printed output from
  return values.

name: eval-str
doc: Evaluates a string of Phel code and returns the result. If the string contains multiple expressions, returns the result of the last one.

name: explain
doc:
Sends a Phel code string to the AI for explanation.

Includes compilation output and namespace context to provide a thorough, grounded explanation.

name: explain-sym
doc: Explains a symbol by sending its source code and documentation to the AI.

name: find-fn
doc: Searches for functions whose name or docstring contains the search string. Returns a vector of maps with :ns, :name, :doc, :private, :min-arity, :max-arity, :is-variadic.

name: find-ns
doc: Returns the namespace name in display form if it is loaded, or nil if no namespace of that name exists. Accepts dot or backslash separators on input.

name: fix
doc: Given Phel code that produced an error, sends both to the AI along with namespace context to suggest a fix.

name: get-source-code
doc: Returns the source code of the definition identified by namespace and name strings, or nil if the source file cannot be found or metadata is missing.

name: get-src-dirs
doc: Returns source directories for namespace resolution: the configured Phel directories plus the current working directory.

name: get-symbol-info
doc:
Returns a hash-map of structured metadata for the definition identified by
  namespace and name strings. Returns nil if no such definition exists.

  Keys: :doc, :file, :line, :column, :end-line, :end-column, :private,
        :deprecated, :min-arity, :max-arity, :is-variadic, :ns, :name

name: intern
doc: Finds or creates a definition named by name-str in namespace ns-str, setting its root value to val when supplied (defaults to nil). The namespace is auto-registered by the underlying `addDefinition` call. Returns the fully qualified symbol (with the namespace in display form).

name: load-file
doc: Loads and evaluates a Phel source file in the current REPL session. Reads the file content and evaluates it using the compiler, preserving the current REPL namespace context. Returns the result of the last expression.

name: load-namespace!
doc:
Loads a namespace from source if not already loaded, restoring the caller's
  current namespace afterwards (evaluating a file switches `*ns*`). Namespaces
  defined directly in the session (no source file) are already loaded and left
  untouched.

name: loaded-namespaces
doc: Returns all namespaces currently loaded in the REPL, in dot-separated display form.

name: macroexpand
doc: Recursively expands the given form until it is no longer a macro call. The form must be quoted to prevent evaluation, matching Clojure semantics.

name: macroexpand-1
doc: Expands the given form once if it is a macro call. The form must be quoted to prevent evaluation, matching Clojure semantics.

name: macroexpand-1-form
doc: Expands the given form once if it is a macro call. Takes a quoted form and returns the expanded form, or the original form unchanged if it is not a macro call. Uses the CompilerFacade to perform the expansion without going through analyze+emit.

name: macroexpand-form
doc: Recursively expands the given form until it is no longer a macro call. Takes a quoted form and returns the fully expanded form. Uses the CompilerFacade to perform the expansion without going through analyze+emit.

name: munge-ns
doc: Encodes a namespace string for registry lookup.

name: normalize-ns-str
doc: Converts backslashes to dots and remaps clojure.* to phel.* when the target exists.

name: normalize-require-symbol
doc: Normalizes a require symbol, returning the original if unchanged.

name: ns-aliases
doc:
Returns a hash-map of {alias => namespace} for all require aliases in the
  given namespace string. Target namespaces are returned in display form.

name: ns-interns
doc:
Returns a hash-map of {name => value} for every definition in the
  given namespace, including private ones. Returns an empty map if the
  namespace has no definitions.

name: ns-list
doc: Returns a sorted vector of all loaded namespace names in display form.

name: ns-publics
doc:
Returns a hash-map of {name => value} for all public definitions in the
  given namespace string. Private definitions are excluded.

name: ns-refers
doc:
Returns a hash-map of {name => source-namespace} for all referred symbols
  in the given namespace string. Source namespaces are returned in display form.

name: phel-expert-preamble
doc: You are a Phel language expert. Phel is a Lisp that compiles to PHP.

name: print-colorful
doc: Prints arguments with colored output.

name: print-colorful-str
doc: Same as print-str from core, but with color.

name: print-tap
doc: Default REPL tap handler: prints a tapped value as `tap> value` with colored output. Registered automatically when the REPL starts, so `(tap> x)` is visible out of the box; detach it with `(remove-tap print-tap)`.

name: println-colorful
doc: Prints arguments with colored output followed by a newline.

name: reload-all!
doc:
Force-reloads every loaded project namespace in dependency order, ignoring
  mtimes. Returns a vector of reloaded namespace names.

name: reload-infos!
doc:
Reloads the given namespace infos (topologically sorted) when their source
  changed or a dependency was reloaded in this pass. When `force?` is true,
  every namespace is reloaded regardless of mtime. Returns a vector of the
  reloaded namespace names in load order.

name: reload!
doc:
Re-evaluates project namespaces whose source files changed since the last
  load, in dependency order, reloading dependents of changed namespaces too.
  The first call (no recorded baseline) reloads every loaded project namespace.
  REPL session state in namespaces without a source file (e.g. `user`) is
  preserved. A compile error is reported and aborts the offending file without
  corrupting already-reloaded namespaces. Returns a vector of reloaded
  namespace names.

name: reloadable-ns-infos
doc:
Returns the NamespaceInformation objects for every loaded project
  namespace, topologically sorted (dependencies first).

name: reloadable?
doc:
A namespace is reloadable from the REPL when it is a project namespace,
  i.e. not one of the bundled `phel.*` standard-library modules.

name: remove-ns
doc: Removes the namespace and all of its definitions from the registry. Use with caution. Returns nil.

name: require
doc:
Requires a Phel module into the environment.
  Accepts both the flat form and the Clojure-compatible vector form:
    (require 'phel\string :as str)
    (require '[phel\string :as str])
    (require '[phel\string :as str :refer [blank?]])

name: review
doc: Sends Phel code to the AI for a code review, including namespace context for awareness of available functions and conventions.

name: run-test
doc:
Runs a single test from the REPL, identified by a fully qualified symbol
  `'my-app.foo-test/my-test`. Loads the namespace if needed. Prints results
  through the default reporter and returns a {:pass :fail :error} summary.

name: run-tests
doc:
Runs all tests in the given namespaces from the REPL, loading each namespace
  first if needed. Each namespace is a symbol, e.g. `'my-app.foo-test`. Prints
  results through the default reporter and returns a {:pass :fail :error}
  summary.

name: run-tests-collecting
doc:
Runs `t/run-tests` with the given options and namespace symbols, preserving
  any outer test state, and returns a {:pass :fail :error} summary.

name: search-doc
doc: Searches docstrings across all loaded namespaces for the given string. Prints matching function names and their documentation.

name: search-ns
doc:
Semantic search over a namespace index built by `embed-ns`.

Returns the k most relevant functions for the query.

name: source
doc: Returns the source code of the given symbol as a string, or nil if unavailable.

name: suggest
doc: Describes what you want to accomplish in natural language and receives Phel code suggestions grounded in available functions.

name: symbol-info
doc:
Returns a hash-map of structured metadata for the given symbol, or nil if
  the symbol cannot be resolved.

  Keys: :doc, :file, :line, :column, :end-line, :end-column, :private,
        :deprecated, :min-arity, :max-arity, :is-variadic, :ns, :name

name: test-ns
doc: Runs all tests in a given namespace from the REPL. Requires the namespace if not already loaded, finds all deftest definitions, runs them, prints results, and returns a hash-map with :pass, :fail, and :error counts. Preserves outer test state so it can be safely called during a test run.

name: use
doc: Adds a use statement to the environment.

name: with-interactive-mode
doc:
Runs `thunk` with `*interactive-mode*` enabled so re-evaluating a definition
  does not trip the duplicate-definition guard, restoring the previous mode
  after. Not `*repl-mode*`: that one also injects the `phel.repl` refers, which
  a reloaded project namespace must not silently gain.

name: build-compiled-router
doc:
Runtime constructor for `compiled-router` expansions. Builds the normalized
   and indexed route tables (which may carry `:handler` functions) from
   `raw-routes` at runtime, pairing them with the Symfony matcher/generator
   tables precompiled at macro-expansion time. Internal — call `compiled-router`.

name: compile-dispatch
doc: Builds a `{route-name → method-dispatch-map}` lookup for all routes.

name: compile-route-dispatch
doc:
For a single `[path data]` route and the global middleware, returns a map
   `{method-kw → [compiled-handler merged-data]}` with an optional `:default`
   entry for the method-agnostic top-level `:handler`.

name: compiled-router
doc:
Like `router` but performs Symfony's route compilation at macro-expansion time. The resulting router uses Symfony's `CompiledUrlMatcher`/`Generator` which are ~3x faster than their dynamic counterparts for large route tables.

Because compilation runs during macro expansion, `raw-routes` must be a literal vector at the call site — it cannot be built from runtime values. Use `router` if your routes are dynamic.

name: dispatch-lookup
doc: Returns `[handler data]` for a given route-name and method, or nil.

name: extract-path-params
doc: Builds a Phel hash-map of path parameters, excluding Symfony's `_route` key.

name: flatten-routes
doc:
Flattens nested routes to a vector of `[path data]` tuples.

  Parent paths are concatenated with their children's paths and parent data
  maps are deep-merged into their children's data. `path-prefix` and
  `common-data` are merged into every route and let you mount a subtree under
  a prefix or share data across all routes.

name: generate-with
doc: Generates a URL using the given Symfony generator.

name: handler
doc:
Builds a `request -> response` function from a router.

  Matching flow per request:

  1. Resolve the request's path via `match-by-path`.
  2. Look up the handler for the request method in the precompiled dispatch
     table, falling back to the route's method-agnostic `:handler`.
  3. Invoke the handler with the request enriched with `[:attributes :match]`
     and `[:attributes :route-data]`. A `nil` response triggers the
     `:not-acceptable` handler.

  Options:

  | key                   | description |
  | ----------------------|-------------|
  | `:middleware`         | global middleware applied to every matched route
  | `:default-handler`    | fallback used for any 404/405/406 case not covered by a specific override
  | `:not-found`          | handler invoked when no route matches (HTTP 404)
  | `:method-not-allowed` | handler invoked when the path matches but no handler exists for the request method (HTTP 405)
  | `:not-acceptable`     | handler invoked when a matched handler returns `nil` (HTTP 406)

  Dispatch is precompiled at handler construction time, so per-request work
  is reduced to two hash-map lookups.

name: indexed-route->match
doc: Converts an `[path data]` tuple from the compiled router's index into a by-name match response. Returns nil when the tuple is nil.

name: match-with
doc:
Runs the given Symfony matcher for `path` and builds a match result using
   `lookup-fn` to resolve `[template data]` for the matched route name.
   Returns nil when no route matches.

name: normalize-routes
doc:
