Parses router `options` (`:path` prefix, `:data` shared-data) and flattens
   `raw-routes` into a vector of `[path data]` tuples. Shared by `router` and
   the runtime side of `compiled-router`.

name: params->php-array
doc: Converts a Phel map of parameters into a PHP associative array keyed by name.

name: route-name-of
doc: Returns the Symfony route name for a `[path data]` tuple, falling back to the path when `:name` isn't provided.

name: router
doc:
Builds a dynamic `Router` from a nested route tree.

  Routes are described as `[path data children*]` where `data` is an optional
  hash-map. Children inherit their parent's path prefix and have parent data
  deep-merged into their own. `data` may contain:

  - `:handler` — a 1-arg `request -> response` function (matches any method)
  - `:middleware` — a vector of `(fn [handler request])` wrappers
  - `:name` — a keyword used for URL generation via `match-by-name` / `generate`
  - method keys (`:get`, `:post`, …) — nested maps with their own `:handler`
    and `:middleware` that apply only for that HTTP method

  `options` accepts `:path` (prefix prepended to every route) and `:data`
  (merged into every route's data).

name: coerce
doc: Walks `schema` and returns `value` with string-typed inputs coerced into their schema-required types. Already-typed values pass through. Unknown or untranslatable values are returned unchanged so validation can report the real failure.

name: conform
doc: Coerces `value` against `schema`. Returns the coerced value if it then validates, otherwise the invalid marker `:phel.schema/invalid`.

name: invalid-marker
doc: Sentinel keyword returned by coercion when a value cannot be coerced to the target schema. Re-exported as `phel.schema/invalid-marker`.

name: explain
doc: Returns `nil` if `value` conforms to `schema`, otherwise a map describing the violations.

name: human-readable-explain
doc: Renders an explain result as a multi-line human string suitable for REPL or CI output. Returns `nil` for a `nil` result.

name: generate
doc:
Generates one random value conforming to `schema`. Accepts the same
  `:size` and `:seed` options as `phel\test\gen/generate`.

name: schema->gen
doc:
Returns a `phel\test\gen` generator for `schema`. Honours a
  `{:gen <gen>}` override in the schema options when present.

name: clear-instrumented!
doc: Removes every instrumentation entry. Returns `nil`.

name: function-schema?
doc:
Returns `true` if `schema` is a function schema of the shape
  `[:=> args-schema return-schema]`.

name: instrument!
doc: Registers `f` under `name` (any key) wrapped with `schema`. Returns the wrapped fn. Subsequent calls to `unstrument!` with the same name can restore the original via `(instrumented-original name)`.

name: instrumented-original
doc:
Returns the original, unwrapped function associated with `name`, or
  `nil` if no instrumentation is registered under `name`.

name: instrumented?
doc: Returns `true` if `name` currently has an instrumentation entry.

name: schema-check?
doc: Returns `true` when runtime validation is enabled.

name: schema?
doc:
Returns `true` if `x` has the shape of a schema value (a keyword or a
  vector whose head is a keyword, including the `:=>` function marker).

name: set-schema-check!
doc:
Enables (`true`) or disables (`false`) runtime validation performed by
  `wrap-with-schema`/`instrument!`. Returns the new value.

name: unstrument!
doc: Unregisters the instrumentation bound to `name` and returns the original (unwrapped) function if present, otherwise `nil`.

name: with-schema-check
doc: Runs thunk `f` with runtime validation set to `enabled?`, restoring the previous value even if `f` throws.

name: wrap-with-function-schema
doc:
Convenience: accepts a `[:=> args-schema return-schema]` schema vector
  and returns `f` wrapped accordingly.

name: wrap-with-schema
doc:
Wraps `f` so each call validates its arguments against `arg-schema`
  (a vector of per-arg schemas) and its return value against
  `return-schema`. When `schema-check?` returns `false` at call time
  the wrapper short-circuits and invokes `f` directly, skipping
  validation on both sides.

name: clear!
doc: Removes every user-registered schema. Returns `nil`.

name: deref-ref
doc: Returns the schema registered under `name`, or `nil` if no schema is registered with that name.

name: register!
doc: Registers `schema` under `name` (usually a keyword). Overwrites any previous entry. Returns the registered schema.

name: registered?
doc: Returns `true` if a schema is registered under `name`.

name: registry-snapshot
doc: Returns the current registry as a plain map. Intended for inspection and testing.

name: unregister!
doc: Removes the schema bound to `name`. Returns `nil`.

name: extract-options
doc: Returns `[options remaining]` where `options` is a map (possibly empty) of trailing options pulled from the second position of a parametric schema, and `remaining` is the rest of the args after the options map.

name: map-entry-optional?
doc:
Returns `true` when a `[:map ...]` entry is declared with
  `{:optional true}`.

name: map-entry-options
doc: Options map for a `[:map ...]` entry `[key opts? schema]`. Returns an empty map when the entry has no options position.

name: map-entry-schema
doc: Inner schema of a `[:map ...]` entry, skipping the options map when present.

name: pattern-source
doc: Returns the raw regex string for a `:re` schema. Accepts either a string pattern (used verbatim) or a compiled PHP regex handle.

name: resolve-or-default
doc: Like `resolve-or-throw`, but returns `default` when `head` is not registered instead of throwing. Used by `coerce` where unknown heads are intentionally passed through unchanged for downstream validation to flag.

name: resolve-or-throw
doc:
Resolves an unknown head by looking it up in the registry. When
  `head` names a registered schema, invokes `f` with the registered
  schema; otherwise throws an `InvalidArgumentException` mentioning
  `label` (e.g. `"unknown schema kind"` or `"no generator for schema kind"`).

  Every head-dispatching caller uses this so the error shape is
  consistent across validator/explainer/coercer/generator.

name: schema-args
doc: Returns the positional arguments of `schema` (children past the head and optional options map).

name: schema-head
doc: Returns the head (kind keyword) of `schema`. Keyword schemas are their own head; vector schemas use their first element.

name: schema-options
doc: Returns the options map of `schema` or `{}` if none.

name: valid-inst?
doc:
PHP has no native instant type; canonical inst values are
  `\DateTimeInterface` instances.

name: valid-seqable?
doc: Collections that `seq` accepts.

name: valid-sequential?
doc: Vectors and lists are sequential.

name: valid?
doc: Returns `true` if `value` conforms to `schema`, otherwise `false`.

name: validate-collection
doc: Generic collection validator used by `[:vector s]` and `[:set s]`.

name: coerce
doc: Walks `schema` and coerces string-shaped input into schema-required types. Idempotent for already-typed values.

name: conform
doc: Coerces `value` against `schema`. Returns the coerced value on success, otherwise `:phel.schema/invalid`.

name: deref-ref
doc: Returns the schema registered under `name`, or `nil`.

name: explain
doc:
Returns `nil` when `value` conforms to `schema`. On mismatch returns
  `{:schema schema :value value :errors [...]}` with one error per
  violation, each carrying `:path`, `:in`, `:schema`, `:value`, `:type`.

name: generate
doc:
Generates a single value conforming to `schema`. Accepts `:size` and
  `:seed` options.

name: human-readable-explain
doc:
Renders an `explain` result as a multi-line human string. Returns
  `nil` for a `nil` input.

name: instrument!
doc: Registers `f` wrapped with `schema` under `name`. Returns the wrapped function. The original is preserved so `unstrument!` can restore it.

name: instrumented?
doc: Returns `true` if `name` is currently instrumented.

name: invalid-marker
doc: Sentinel value (`:phel.schema/invalid`) returned by `conform` when a value cannot be coerced to fit a schema. `conform` returns this marker instead of throwing, so compare against it to detect failure.

name: register!
doc: Registers `schema` under `name` in the global schema registry.

name: registered?
doc: Returns `true` if a schema is registered under `name`.

name: schema->gen
doc: Returns the `phel\test\gen` generator associated with `schema`.

name: schema-args
doc: Returns the positional arguments of `schema` (children past the head and optional options map).

name: schema-check?
doc: Returns `true` when runtime validation performed by the instrument helpers is currently enabled.

name: schema-head
doc: Returns the dispatch head (kind keyword) of `schema`.

name: schema-options
doc: Returns the options map of `schema` or `{}`.

name: schema?
doc: Returns `true` if `x` has the shape of a schema value.

name: set-schema-check!
doc: Enables (`true`) or disables (`false`) runtime validation. Returns the new value.

name: unregister!
doc: Removes the schema bound to `name`. Returns `nil`.

name: unstrument!
doc: Removes the instrumentation registered under `name` and returns the original, unwrapped function (or `nil` if no entry).

name: validate
doc: Returns `true` if `value` conforms to `schema`, otherwise `false`.

name: with-schema-check
doc:
Invokes zero-arg thunk `f` with runtime validation forced to
  `enabled?`. The previous value is restored on return or exception.

name: wrap-with-function-schema
doc: Wraps `f` with the `[:=> args ret]` function schema.

name: wrap-with-schema
doc: Wraps `f` so calls validate arguments and return values against the supplied schemas.

name: as-pattern
doc: Returns slash-delimited patterns as-is and wraps other strings as literals.

name: ascii-blank-chars
doc: x0Bfx1Cx1Dx1Ex1F

name: assert-string
doc:
Throws `InvalidArgumentException` unless `x` is a string. Guards the PHP
  string builtins these functions delegate to, which would otherwise leak a
  raw `Passing null to parameter ... of type string is deprecated` warning
  (a hard `TypeError` in PHP 9) and return nonsense on non-string input.

  `:inline` because this runs on nearly every call into this namespace, and
  some functions assert twice. As a `defn-` each guard cost a registry lookup
  before it could look at the value; inlined it is an `is_string` test, and
  only the failing path resolves a function.

name: blank?
doc: True if s is nil, empty, or contains only whitespace. Non-breaking separators (`U+00A0`, `U+2007`, `U+202F`) are not treated as whitespace.

name: capitalize
doc: Converts first character to upper-case and all other characters to lower-case.

name: chars
doc:
Returns a vector of characters from string s.

This is a convenience function for converting strings to character sequences. Properly handles multibyte UTF-8 characters.

name: contains?
doc: True if s contains substr. Synonym for `includes?`.

name: ends-with?
doc: True if s ends with substr.

name: escape
doc: Returns a new string with each character escaped according to cmap.

name: includes?
doc: True if s includes substr.

name: index-of
doc: Returns the index of the first occurrence of value in s, or nil if not found. The optional from-index sets where the search begins; a negative from-index counts back from the end of s.

name: join
doc: Returns a string of all elements in coll, separated by an optional separator.

name: last-index-of
doc: Returns the index of the last occurrence of value in s, or nil if not found. The optional from-index sets the upper bound for the match; a negative from-index counts back from the end of s.

name: lower-case
doc: Converts string to all lower-case.

name: pad-both
doc: Returns a string padded on both sides to length len.

name: pad-left
doc: Returns a string padded on the left side to length len.

name: pad-or-space
doc:
The pad string to use, defaulting to a single space. An empty (or nil) pad
  string would make PHP's `str_pad` raise an uncatchable argument error.

name: pad-right
doc: Returns a string padded on the right side to length len.

name: pattern-error
doc:
Diagnoses a `preg_split` failure. Reached only when PCRE has already
  rejected the pattern, so nothing here runs on a successful split.

  The common mistake is a bare separator such as " ", which PCRE reads as an
  empty pattern between two space delimiters; that is worth naming separately
  from a pattern that is delimited but malformed.

name: re-quote-replacement
doc: Escapes special characters in a replacement string for literal use.

name: repeat
doc: Returns a string containing n copies of s.

name: replace
doc:
Replaces all instances of match with replacement in s. Plain string matches
  are literal; use a regex literal for regular-expression matching.

name: replace-first
doc:
Replaces the first instance of match with replacement in s. Plain string
  matches are literal; use a regex literal for regular-expression matching.

name: reverse
doc: Returns s with its characters reversed.

name: split
doc: Splits string on a regular expression, returning a vector of parts.

name: split-lines
doc: Splits s on \n or \r\n. Trailing empty lines are not returned.

name: starts-with?
doc: True if s starts with substr.

name: string-expected
doc:
The throwing half of `assert-string`, kept out of line so the guard itself
  compiles to a bare `is_string` test.

name: subs
doc: Returns the substring of s from start (inclusive) to end (exclusive).

name: trim
doc: Removes whitespace from both ends of string.

name: trim-newline
doc: Removes all trailing newline or return characters from string.

name: triml
doc: Removes whitespace from the left side of string.

name: trimr
doc: Removes whitespace from the right side of string.

name: upper-case
doc: Converts string to all upper-case.

name: boolean
doc: Generator of booleans.

name: char
doc: Generator of printable ASCII characters (space through `~`).

name: char-alpha
doc: Generator of ASCII letters.

name: char-alphanumeric
doc: Generator of ASCII letters and digits.

name: choose
doc: Generator of integers in the closed interval `[lo hi]`.

name: default-num-tests
doc: Number of trials `quick-check` runs by default.

name: default-size
doc: Magnitude used when no `:size` option is supplied.

name: defspec
doc:
Defines a property test. The generated `deftest` runs `quick-check`
  and asserts the result is `:pass`. `options` is a hash-map accepting
  `:num-tests`, `:size`, `:seed` and `:shrink?`.

  Attach `^:no-shrink` metadata to the name to skip shrinking on
  failure. The `test-name` symbol's metadata is also forwarded to the
  underlying `deftest`, so tag-based selectors apply as usual.

  On failure a `:defspec-failed` event is sent to the reporter set
  before the surrounding `is` assertion records a `:failed` event.
  Reporters that want rich shrink information can subscribe to it; the
  built-in reporters keep rendering their usual failure summary.

  Shape: `(defspec name options args-gen property)`.

name: elements
doc: Generator that picks a random element from `coll`.

name: emit-spec-failure-event!
doc: Fans out a `:defspec-failed` event carrying the rich outcome map so reporters can surface the shrunk counterexample, seed, and shrink step count.

name: float
doc: Generator of floats in `[0, 1)`.

name: fmap
doc: Returns a generator that applies `f` to values produced by `g`.

name: frequency
doc: Generator that picks one of the `[weight gen]` pairs with probability proportional to weight.

name: generate
doc: Runs `g` once and returns a single value. Accepts `:size` and `:seed`.

name: int
doc: Generator of integers in `[-size, size]`.

name: keyword
doc: Generator of keywords with alphabetic names, length in `[1, max(1, size)]`.

name: large-int
doc: Generator of arbitrary PHP-range integers.

name: list-of
doc: Generator of lists whose elements come from `g`. Length in `[0, size]`.

name: map-of
doc: Generator of hash-maps with keys from `kg` and values from `vg`. Number of entries is in `[0, size]`.

name: nat
doc: Generator of non-negative integers in `[0, size]`.

name: one-of
doc: Generator that selects uniformly from `gens` and runs the chosen one.

name: quick-check
doc:
Runs `property` for `num-tests` trials, drawing each trial's arguments from
  `args-gen` (a generator returning a vector of arguments). Returns a hash-map
  with `:result` (`:pass`, `:failed`, or `:error`), `:num-tests`, and the
  effective `:seed` for replay. On failure/error the failing `:args` (and
  `:exception`) are also included.

  Options:
  - `:size` (default 100): magnitude passed to the generator.
  - `:seed` (default: fresh per-run): PRNG seed.
  - `:shrink?` (default: true): when true, a failing trial is shrunk to
    a minimal counterexample; the resulting map carries `:shrunk-args`,
    `:original-args` and `:shrink-steps`.
example: (quick-check 50 (tuple int int) (fn [a b] (= (+ a b) (+ b a))))
arities: (quick-check num-tests args-gen property {:size size, :seed seed, :shrink? shrink?})

name: resize
doc: Returns a generator equivalent to `g` but with `size` forced to `n`.

name: return
doc: Generator that always yields `x`.

name: sample
doc: Runs `g` `num-samples` times (default 10) and returns a vector of values. Accepts `:size` and `:seed`.

name: set-of
doc: Generator of hash-sets with elements from `g`. Cardinality in `[0, size]`.

name: shrink-outcome
doc: Given a failing trial `outcome`, runs the shrink driver on its args and returns an outcome augmented with `:original-args`, `:shrunk-args` and `:shrink-steps`. If `shrink?` is falsy, returns `outcome` unchanged.

name: sized
doc: Builds a generator from a function `f` of `size`. The returned generator forwards its `size` into `f`, which must yield another generator that is then invoked with the same size.

name: spec-failure-message
doc: Renders the human-readable failure message for a `defspec` outcome map. Includes the shrink summary when the trial's arguments were shrunk to a smaller counterexample.

name: string
doc: Generator of printable ASCII strings, length in `[0, size]`.

name: string-alpha
doc: Generator of ASCII alphabetic strings, length in `[0, size]`.

name: string-alphanumeric
doc: Generator of ASCII alphanumeric strings, length in `[0, size]`.

name: such-that
doc:
Generator yielding only values from `g` that satisfy `pred`. Retries up to
  `max-tries` (default 100) before throwing.

name: symbol
doc: Generator of symbols with alphabetic names, length in `[1, max(1, size)]`.

name: tuple
doc: Generator of a fixed-length vector produced by running each of the given generators in order. Accepts either a vector of generators or variadic generator arguments.

name: vector-of
doc:
Generator of vectors. Length is `[0, size]` with one arg, exactly `n` with
  `(vector-of g n)`, or `[lo, hi]` with `(vector-of g lo hi)`.

name: int-rose-tree
doc: Rose tree for an integer `n` that shrinks toward zero.

name: int-rose-tree-towards
doc: Rose tree for `n` whose children shrink strictly toward `target`.

name: lazy-concat
doc: One-element-at-a-time concatenation of two lazy seqs.

name: lazy-filter
doc: One-element-at-a-time `filter`.

name: lazy-map
doc: Element-wise `(map f coll)` that realises one element at a time. Necessary because the built-in `map` realises a full chunk at once, which is incompatible with the self-recursive rose-tree structure.

name: positional-shrinks
doc: For index `i`, emits a lazy seq of variants of `trees` where only position `i` has been replaced with each of its shrinks.

name: rose-bind
doc: Monadic bind. `f` takes a value and returns a rose tree; the resulting tree combines the shrinks of `t` (each fed through `f`) with the shrinks produced by `f` on the root.

name: rose-children
doc: Returns the lazy sequence of immediate child rose trees.

name: rose-filter
doc:
Returns the subtree consisting only of nodes whose value satisfies
  `pred`. Children that fail `pred` are pruned. If the root fails
  `pred`, returns `nil` (caller is responsible for handling).

name: rose-fmap
doc: Applies `f` to every value in rose tree `t` (the root and, lazily, every descendant).

name: rose-join
doc: Flattens a rose tree of rose trees into a single rose tree.

name: rose-map
doc:
Rose tree for a hash-map. `entry-trees` is a vector of rose trees of
  `[k v]` pairs. Shrinks by removing entries and by shrinking each
  pair in place.

name: rose-pure
doc: Leaf rose tree: value `x` with no shrink candidates.

name: rose-root
doc: Returns the root value of rose tree `t`.

name: rose-shrinks
doc: Alias for `rose-children`: the lazy sequence of immediate smaller variants of the current root.

name: rose-string
doc: Rose tree for a string whose elements are char rose trees.

name: rose-tree
doc: Rose tree constructor. `children` should be a lazy sequence of rose trees (or any seqable value).

name: rose-vector
doc: Rose tree for a vector whose children are built from the rose trees of its elements. Shrinks by removing elements and by shrinking each element in place.

name: rose-vector-lax
doc: Like `rose-vector` but preserves original length; only shrinks each element in place (no removal).

name: rose-zip
doc: Takes a vector of rose trees and returns a rose tree whose root is the vector of roots and whose children shrink one position at a time.

name: rose?
doc: Returns `true` if `x` looks like a rose tree.

name: shrink-int
doc: Shrink strategy toward zero: halving steps (`n/2`, `n/4`, …) and then decrement toward zero.

name: shrink-int-towards
doc:
Returns a seq of integer candidates strictly closer to `target` than
  `n`. Yields the target first, then halving steps.

name: shrink-vector-by-removal
doc: Candidates formed by dropping a leading block of halving sizes, then single-element drops.

name: shrinks-of-many
doc: Given a vector of rose trees, returns a lazy sequence of rose-tree vectors where each vector shrinks exactly one of the inputs in turn.

name: shrinks-of-many*
doc: Helper: lazily iterates each position in turn.

name: compile-filter-regex
doc: Wraps a user-supplied regex body in PCRE delimiters when it is not already a `/.../` pattern. Treats bare fragments as substring matchers.

name: glob->regex
doc: Converts a namespace glob (`phel.http.*`) into an anchored PCRE pattern. `.` is treated literally, `*` matches any run of non-`.` characters, `**` matches anything. The glob is case-sensitive.

name: has-selectors?
doc: Returns `true` when `options` contains at least one non-empty selector key.

name: has-tag?
doc: Returns `true` when `meta` carries `tag` (a keyword or a string treated as a keyword). Single-keyword metadata (`^:integration`) and map-based multi-tag metadata (`^{:tags [:integration :slow]}`) both match.

name: keep-test?
doc: Returns `true` when the test described by `meta` and `ns-name` should be run under `options`. `options` is a map that may carry any of `:include`, `:exclude`, `:ns-patterns`, `:filters`. Selectors that are absent or empty impose no restriction; specified selectors are AND'd together.

name: matches-exclude?
doc: Returns `true` when any tag in `excludes` is truthy on `meta`. An empty or nil `excludes` vector always returns `false` (nothing excluded).

name: matches-filter?
doc: Returns `true` when `patterns` is empty (no restriction) or when any entry in `patterns` matches `test-name`.

name: matches-include?
doc: Returns `true` when `includes` is empty (no restriction) or when any tag in `includes` is truthy on `meta`.

name: matches-ns?
doc: Returns `true` when `patterns` is empty (no restriction) or when any glob in `patterns` matches `ns-name`.

name: name-matches?
doc: Returns `true` when `pattern` (a PCRE `/.../` string or a plain substring) matches `test-name`.

name: non-empty-vec?
doc: Returns `true` when `xs` is a non-nil, non-empty vector/seq. Used to check whether a selector option was supplied by the caller.

name: normalize-ns
doc:
Normalizes a namespace name so both `phel\test\foo` and
  `phel.test.foo` are interchangeable for glob matching.

name: ns-matches?
doc:
Returns `true` when `ns-name` matches the glob `pattern`. Supports
  `*` (single segment) and `**` (any run). Backslash-separated
  namespaces (`phel\http\client`) are treated as dotted
  (`phel.http.client`) so globs stay portable.

name: tag-key
doc: Coerces a selector tag (keyword or string) into the keyword form used to look up metadata. Returns `nil` for other inputs.

name: truthy-tag?
doc: True when `meta` contains a truthy value at `kw`. Also accepts vector-valued `:tags` metadata, checking membership by keyword.

name: args->rose
doc: Rose tree whose root is `args` and children shrink each positional argument in place using its value-based shrinker. Arguments are never dropped (they are function parameters, not collection elements).

name: fails?
doc: Returns `true` when `pred` fails for `value` (either returning a non-truthy result or throwing).

name: shrink
doc:
Walks rose tree `tree` depth-first, greedily descending into any
  child whose root still fails `pred`. Returns
  `{:smallest v :shrink-steps n :tree final-tree}`.

name: shrink-args
doc:
Shrinks a failing args vector using `property`. Returns
  `{:smallest args :shrink-steps n}` where `args` is the smallest args
  vector that still makes `property` fail.

name: value->rose
doc: Builds a rose tree for `v` using the built-in shrink strategy that matches its runtime type. Integers shrink toward zero; strings, vectors, lists, hash-maps and sets shrink by element removal plus recursive element shrinks; everything else is a leaf.

name: *testing-contexts*
doc: Stack of testing context strings, most recent first.

name: add-reporter!
doc: Appends `reporter-fn` to the active reporter set. Returns the updated reporter list.

name: announce-seed!
doc: Prints `Seed: <n>` once at the start of a randomized run so failures can be reproduced with `--seed=<n>`.

name: are
doc:
Checks multiple assertions with a template expression.
  `argv` is a vector of template variables, `expr` is the assertion template,
  and the remaining `args` are partitioned by `(count argv)` to fill the template.
  Template variables are substituted lexically at macro-expansion time, so
  literal collection cells (e.g. `()`, `[]`, `{}`) are preserved as data and
  are not evaluated as code.

name: assert-expr
doc:
Public extension point for the `is` macro: an open multimethod dispatched on
  the first symbol of the asserted form (or `:default` for non-list forms and for
  lists not starting with a symbol).

  Extend it with `(defmethod phel.test/assert-expr 'my-form [message form] ...)`,
  returning a quoted form for `is` to evaluate. Methods must be loaded before any
  `is` form using their dispatch value is expanded.

name: bump-junit-counters
doc:
Increments `:tests`, plus `:failures`/`:errors` based on the event's
  `:state`. Used to aggregate both the per-suite and per-run totals.

name: clear-reporters!
doc: Removes every registered reporter. Returns an empty vector.

name: coerce-reporter
doc: Turns a single `:reporters` entry (function, keyword, or string) into a reporter function. Throws on unknown names or invalid values.

name: collection-diff-applicable?
doc: Returns true when a `=`/`not=` failure carries two same-shape collections that actually differ. Same-shape rules out scalar pairs (a `1`/`2` diff is noise); the `not=` check rules out a `not=` failure's equal pair, which would render an empty diff.

name: compose-two-fixtures
doc: Returns a fixture that applies f1 around a fixture that applies f2 around g.

name: decorate-event
doc: Prepends testing-context information to the event message and injects the current test name.

name: default-fixture
doc: Identity fixture: just invokes the wrapped function.

name: default-reporter
doc: Human-readable dot output. Preserves the legacy behavior: `.` for pass, `F` for fail, `E` for error, plus periodic newlines so long runs wrap at 80 columns. `S` marks a skipped test.

name: deftest
doc:
Defines a test function.

Metadata attached to `test-name` is forwarded to the defined function so selectors can inspect it at runtime. `^:integration` (shorthand for `{:integration true}`) and `^{:tags [:integration :slow]}` multi-tag maps are both honoured.

name: do-report
doc: Add file and line information to a test result and call report. If you are writing a custom assert-expr method, call this function to pass test results to report.

name: dot-reporter
doc:
Minimal CI-friendly reporter. Prints `.` per pass, `F` per failure,
  `E` per error, `S` per skipped test, and a compact one-line summary
  at the end. Does not print failure/error diagnostics.

name: emit-marker!
doc: Prints a single progress marker and wraps the line every 80 markers.

name: emit-summary!
doc: Emits the `:summary` event for the current stats to the active reporter set.

name: escape-for-string-diff
doc: Escapes backslashes, quotes, and control whitespace so every character renders one-or-more visible columns and the caret stays aligned.

name: find-test-vars
doc: Discovers every `deftest`-defined function in `ns` and returns a vector of `{:fn <callable> :meta <map>}` entries. The caller is responsible for applying selectors.

name: first-mismatch-index
doc: 0-based index of the first differing character between strings `a` and `b`. When one string is a prefix of the other, the mismatch is the length of the shorter one. Returns nil for equal strings.

name: generate-seed
doc: Returns a fresh non-negative integer seed suitable for PHP's RNG.

name: get-failed-tests
doc: Returns the names (`ns/test-name`) of tests that failed or errored in the last run. Used by `--parallel` orchestration to aggregate last-failed lists across worker processes.

name: get-reporters
doc: Returns the currently registered reporter functions as a vector.

name: get-stats
doc: Returns the current test statistics as a hash-map with :failed and :counts keys.

name: is
doc: Asserts that an expression is true.

name: join-fixtures
doc: Composes a collection of fixtures into a single fixture function.

name: junit-ensure-current
doc: Ensures `state` has a `:current` suite; lazily initialised from the event's `:ns` when a testcase arrives outside a `begin-test-ns`.

name: junit-reporter
doc:
JUnit-XML v1 output. Emits a `<testsuites>` root with one
  `<testsuite>` per Phel namespace. Each assertion becomes a
  `<testcase>`; failures and errors are nested accordingly.

name: legacy-filter-matches?
doc: Back-compat: the original `--filter` option accepted a single substring matched against the test name. When selectors are also active, this check still applies so existing callers keep behaving.

name: maybe-shuffle-tests
doc: Returns `tests` shuffled when `:random-order` is set in `options` (or an explicit `:seed` is supplied), or unchanged otherwise. The active seed (`:seed-resolved`) reseeds PHP's Mersenne Twister so the resulting order is reproducible.

name: only-tests-matches?
doc:
Returns true when `only-tests` is empty (no restriction) or when
  `ns/test-name` matches one of the entries verbatim.

name: partition-tests
doc:
Splits the discovered tests into a `{:keep [...] :skip [...]}` map
  using the selector options. `:keep` preserves original order; each
  `:skip` entry is annotated with its metadata so reporters can surface
  skip events.

name: print-collection-diff
doc:
Prints a unified-diff-like block comparing the `expected` and `actual`
  collections. Maps show added/removed/changed keys with `+`, `-`, `~`;
  vectors and lists show index-aligned `+`, `-`, ` ` rows; sets show the
  symmetric difference. Callers should invoke this only after checking
  `same-shape?` and `diff-worth-rendering?`.

name: print-form-evaluated
doc: Prints the `Form: ... / evaluated to: ...` pair shared by every failure printer that reports a single value and its computed result.

name: print-label
doc: Prints `label:`, the readable form of `value`, then any extra trailing words on a single line. Used by the built-in failure printers to keep the right-aligned two-column layout consistent.

name: print-string-diff
doc: Prints a windowed expected/actual pair with a caret under the first differing character. Supplements the summary line for `=` failures over two strings.

name: quote-if-empty-list
doc: Wraps an empty-list cell in `(quote ())` so it survives compilation as literal data. Phel's evaluator cannot apply an empty list as a call, so a bare `()` placed in value position (e.g. as an `are` template cell) must be quoted for the generated code to compile. Non-empty lists and other values are returned unchanged — the caller can quote explicitly if needed.

name: record-stats!
doc: Mutates the internal stats atom based on an assertion-result event.

name: register-reporter!
doc: Registers a custom reporter function under `name` (keyword or keyword-castable string). Returns `name`.

name: repeat-count
doc: Returns the validated `:repeat` count from `options`, defaulting to 1.

name: report
doc:
Records a test-framework event and dispatches it to the active
  reporters. `data` must contain a `:type` key (`:pass`, `:failed`,
  `:error`, `:begin-test-ns`, `:end-test-ns`, `:begin-test-run`,
  `:summary`, or a user-defined event). The default methods for
  assertion outcomes update the internal stats and invoke every
  registered reporter. Other event types flow straight through to the
  reporter set. Extend by registering
  `(defmethod report :custom-type [event] ...)`.

name: requested-reporters
doc:
Returns the user-selected reporter identifiers, honouring the
  `--testdox` shortcut and defaulting to `[:default]`.

name: reset-stats
doc: Resets the test statistics to their initial state. Call this before running a new batch of tests to get fresh results.

name: resolve-reporter
doc: Returns the reporter function registered for `name` (keyword or string). Checks user-registered reporters before the built-in set. Returns `nil` if the name is unknown.

name: resolve-reporters-option
doc: Resolves the `:reporters` option into a vector of reporter functions. Accepts a sequence of keywords or strings (built-in names), or a sequence of functions, or a mix. Defaults to `[:default]`.

name: resolve-seed
doc: Returns the seed `run-tests` should use, or `nil` when ordering is deterministic and no seed was requested. An explicit `:seed` always wins; `:random-order` without a seed gets a freshly generated one.

name: restore-stats
doc: Restores test statistics from a previously saved state.

name: run-tests
doc:
Runs all tests in the given namespaces. When `:list-only` is true,
  prints the discovered tests and skips execution.

  Recognized option keys include `:filter`, `:filters`, `:include`,
  `:exclude`, `:ns-patterns`, `:fail-fast`, `:stack-trace`, `:reporters`,
  `:junit-output`, `:list-only`, `:only-tests`, `:last-failed-file`,
  `:slowest`, `:repeat` (run the selected tests N times), `:seed`
  (integer seed for the order RNG), and `:random-order` (shuffle tests
  per namespace).

name: same-shape?
doc: Returns true when `a` and `b` are both maps, both sets, or both sequential. Mixed-shape pairs fall back to the summary printer.

name: selector-options
doc: Extracts the tag/namespace selector subset from the full options map. Name-based filters (`:filter` / `:filters`) are handled separately as discovery filters and are intentionally excluded here.

name: sequential?
doc: Returns true when `v` is a vector or a list: the two ordered shapes the diff renderer aligns by index.

name: set-junit-output!
doc: Configures the output path the JUnit reporter writes to. When `nil`, the XML is printed to stdout.

name: set-reporters!
doc: Replaces the active reporter set with `reporters` (a sequence of single-argument functions). Returns the new reporter list.

name: skip-reason
doc:
Returns `:selector` when the test is excluded by a tag or namespace
  selector, or `nil` when it should run. Name-based filters
  (`:filter` / `:filters`) are applied upstream as discovery filters and
  never reach this function.

name: sort-by-readable
doc: Sorts `coll` by the readable representation of each entry. Used to give the diff a deterministic order even when keys or values mix types that Phel's default comparator rejects.

name: string-diff-window
doc: Renders string `s` windowed from `start` to just past mismatch index `idx` (plus trailing context), quoted and escaped, with `...` markers for clipped ends. Returns [rendered caret-column] where caret-column points at the mismatch within the rendered text.

name: substitute-symbols
doc: Recursively replaces every occurrence of a key in `smap` within `form` with its corresponding value, walking lists, vectors, hash-maps, and hash-sets. Used by `are` to expand template cells at macro-expansion time rather than let-binding them at runtime.

name: successful?
doc: Checks if all tests passed.

name: tap-reporter
doc: TAP v13 output. Emits `TAP version 13`, `1..N` plan, `ok`/`not ok` lines per assertion, and a YAML block per failure. `N` is the total number of assertions observed during the run.

name: testdox-reporter
doc: Per-assertion single-line description used by the `--reporter=testdox` flag.

name: testing
doc: Adds a testing context string. Used inside deftest to describe a group of assertions. The context string is prepended to failure messages for better diagnostics.

name: use-fixtures
doc:
Registers fixture functions for the current namespace.

  `fixture-type` is either `:each` (wraps every individual test) or
  `:once` (wraps the whole run in a single function). Each fixture is
  a function of one argument — a thunk `(fn [])` representing the tests
  to run — and is expected to invoke that thunk somewhere in its body.

  Calling `use-fixtures` with no fixture functions removes all fixtures
  of that type previously registered on the namespace.

name: visible-test-pred
doc: Returns the predicate that decides whether a discovered test passes the discovery filters (`:filter`, `:filters`, `:only-tests`).

name: visible-tests-for-ns
doc:
Returns the discovered tests in `ns` that survive the discovery filters
  (`:filter`, `:filters`, `:only-tests`). Tag and namespace selectors are
  applied later by `partition-tests` so they can surface as skip events.
  Honours `:random-order` to shuffle the result deterministically.

name: with-isolated-reporters
doc: Installs `reporters` as the only active reporter set while `body` runs, then restores the previously registered reporters. Returns the value of the last form in `body`. Use it to capture the events a piece of code emits without permanently replacing the reporters the surrounding run relies on. The previous reporter set is restored even when `body` throws.

name: with-isolated-stats
doc: Runs `body` against a freshly reset statistics accumulator and returns the stats map that `body` produced, then restores the statistics the caller had before. Use it when asserting on the outcome of assertions under test, so their pass/fail counts never leak into the surrounding run. Wrap `body` in `with-output-buffer` to swallow the reporter output those assertions emit. The caller's statistics are restored even when `body` throws.

name: write-last-failed!
doc:
Persists the failed-test list to `path` so a subsequent
  `--last-failed` run can replay it. Always overwrites; an empty list
  produces an empty file.

name: deftrace
doc: Like `defn`, but every call to the defined function prints its arguments and result via `trace-fn`. Recursive calls are traced too. Supports an optional docstring and metadata map like `defn`.
example:
(deftrace fact [n] (if (<= n 1) 1 (* n (fact (dec n)))))
(fact 2)
; TRACE t1: (fact 2)
; TRACE t2: | (fact 1)
; TRACE t2: | => 1
; TRACE t1: => 2

name: dotrace
doc: Temporarily traces the given global functions while `body` runs, then restores them. `fn-syms` is a vector of symbols naming global functions. Process-global like `with-redefs`, so intended for debugging and tests, not concurrent production code.
example:
(defn add [a b] (+ a b))
(dotrace [add] (add 1 2))
; TRACE t1: (add 1 2)
; TRACE t1: => 3

name: reset-trace-state!
doc: Resets the trace depth and the trace id counter to their initial values. Useful to make trace output deterministic in tests.

name: trace
doc: Prints `value` to the standard error stream and returns it unchanged. With a `tag`, prints `TRACE tag: value`; without, prints `TRACE: value`. Like `dbg` but without source-location capture, so it also works when composed point-free.

name: trace-fn
doc: Returns a function that behaves like `f` but prints every call with its arguments and its result to the standard error stream. Nested calls of traced functions are indented by depth and numbered, so recursion and call chains stay readable. `fn-name` is the label used in the output.
example:
(def fib-t (trace-fn "fib" fib))
(fib-t 2)
; TRACE t1: (fib 2)
; TRACE t2: | (fib 1)
; TRACE t2: | => 1
; TRACE t1: => 1

name: decode
doc: Recursive Transit decoder over a `json_decode` result tree.

name: decode-array
doc: Decodes a JSON array. Detects `["~#tag", rep]` markers before falling back to a positional vector decode.

name: decode-cmap
doc: Decodes a `~#cmap` payload — a flat sequence of alternating key/value representations — into a persistent map.

name: decode-object
doc: Decodes a JSON object (as PHP associative array) into a Phel map. String keys may themselves be Transit-encoded (e.g. `"~:foo"`).

name: decode-tagged-array
doc:
Decodes a `["~#tag", rep]` array. Handles built-in collection tags
  (`set`, `list`, `cmap`) and falls back to `:handlers` / `:default-handler`.

name: decode-tagged-scalar
doc: Decodes a `~`-prefixed string. Returns the decoded value, or the original string when the prefix is one of the escape forms.

name: encode
doc:
Encodes a Phel value into the PHP-array shape consumed by
  `json_encode`. Strings carrying a Transit-sensitive prefix are
  escaped with a leading `~`.

name: encode-sequential
doc: Encodes each element of `coll` into a PHP array. When `tag` is non-nil the array is wrapped as a Transit tagged array (e.g. "~#set"); a nil `tag` yields a bare array.

name: escape-string
doc:
Escapes a plain Phel string so that an existing leading `~`, `^`, or
  `` ` `` is not mistaken for a Transit tag by the reader.

name: read-string
doc:
Reads one Transit+JSON-Verbose value from string `s`.

  Options:
    :handlers         map of tag-string to 1-arg fn for `~#tag` extensions
    :default-handler  2-arg fn `(fn [tag rep] ...)` invoked for any
                      unknown tag (both scalar and array forms). Receives
                      the bare tag name (e.g. "point", ":", "~") and
                      the already-decoded representation.

name: starts-with?
doc: True when `s` begins with the single character `c`.

name: string-keys?
doc:
True when `m` is non-empty and every key is a plain Phel string. An empty
  map is excluded so it round-trips through the `~#cmap` form instead of an
  empty JSON array (which would decode back as a vector).

name: tag-string
doc: Returns the tag portion of a `~#tag`-encoded array marker, or nil when `s` is not such a marker.

name: write-string
doc: Serialises `value` to a Transit+JSON-Verbose string.

name: keywordize-keys
doc: Recursively transforms all string keys in hash-maps to keywords.

name: postwalk
doc: Performs a depth-first, post-order traversal of `form`. Calls `f` on each sub-form, uses `f`'s return value in place of the original. Walks into vectors, lists, hash-maps, and hash-sets.

name: postwalk-replace
doc:
Recursively transforms `form` by replacing every occurrence of a key in
  `smap` with the corresponding value. Applies replacements bottom-up.

name: prewalk
doc: Like `postwalk`, but does a pre-order traversal (applies `f` before recursing into children).

name: prewalk-replace
doc:
Recursively transforms `form` by replacing every occurrence of a key in
  `smap` with the corresponding value. Applies replacements top-down.

name: stringify-keys
doc: Recursively transforms all keyword keys in hash-maps to strings.

name: walk
doc: Traverses `form`, an arbitrary data structure. Applies `inner` to each element of `form`, building up a data structure of the same type, then applies `outer` to the result. Recognizes vectors, lists, hash-maps, and hash-sets. Other types are returned as-is.

name: clear-on-reload
doc: Removes every hook registered for `namespace`.

name: register-on-reload
doc: Registers a zero-arg function to run every time `namespace` is reloaded by the watcher. Replaces any previously registered hook with the same `name`.

name: run-on-reload-hooks
doc: Executes every hook registered for `namespace`. Returns the number of hooks that fired.

name: watch!
doc: Starts the file watcher on the given vector of paths. Blocks until the watcher is stopped (e.g. Ctrl+C). Reloads changed namespaces in dependency order and runs any hooks registered with `register-on-reload`.
